Unit 1 Lateral Earth Pressure 0/6
Q.1 (a) 2025 2M Theory 3x
What are different Types of Earth Pressure and what are different theories of Earth Pressures?
1. Types of Earth Pressure:
1.
Active Earth Pressure: Lateral pressure exerted by soil when the retaining wall moves away from the backfill, allowing shear resistance to mobilize towards the wall.
Example: A cantilever retaining wall tilting outwards away from the fill.
2.
Passive Earth Pressure: Maximum lateral resistance exerted by soil when the retaining wall pushes into the backfill.
Example: Soil resisting the front toe of a retaining wall or an embedded anchor block.
3.
Earth Pressure at Rest: Lateral pressure exerted by soil against a rigid, unyielding wall undergoing zero lateral strain (εx = 0).
Example: Rigid basement retaining walls or massive bridge abutments keyed into rock.
2. Theories of Earth Pressure:
1.
Rankine's Theory: Considers the stress state of plastic equilibrium in a semi-infinite, homogeneous, cohesionless soil mass behind a smooth, vertical wall.
2.
Coulomb's Wedge Theory: Considers the static equilibrium of a sliding wedge of soil behaving as a rigid body along a plane failure surface, accounting for wall friction (δ) and batter/sloping backfill.
Q.1 (b) i 2025 3M Numerical 2x
A smooth vertical wall, 6 m high supports an inclined non cohesive backfill (φ = 32°; γ = 21 kN/m³) at an angle 10° with horizontal. Compute the total active & passive pressure at the bottom of wall.
Given Parameters:
Wall height H = 6 m, φ = 32°, γ = 21 kN/m³, surcharge slope β = 10°, smooth vertical wall.
1.
Trigonometric Quantities:
$$\cos \beta = \cos 10^\circ = 0.9848, \cos \phi = \cos 32^\circ = 0.8480$$

$$\sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi } = \sqrt{0.9848^2 - 0.8480^2} = \sqrt{0.9698 - 0.7192} = \sqrt{0.2507} = 0.5007$$
2.
Rankine Earth Pressure Coefficients:
$$K_a = \cos \beta \cdot \frac{\cos \beta - \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi}}{\cos \beta + \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi}} = 0.9848 \cdot \frac{0.9848 - 0.5007}{0.9848 + 0.5007} = \frac{0.4767}{1.4855} = \mathbf{0.3210}$$

$$K_p = \cos \beta \cdot \frac{\cos \beta + \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi}}{\cos \beta - \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi}} = 0.9848 \cdot \frac{0.9848 + 0.5007}{0.9848 - 0.5007} = \frac{1.4629}{0.4841} = \mathbf{3.0219}$$
3. Pressure Intensities at Bottom of Wall (z = 6 m):
•
Total Active Earth Pressure:
$$p_a = K_a \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 0.3210 \times 21 \times 6 = \mathbf{40.45\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
(inclined at β = 10° to horizontal).
•
Total Passive Earth Pressure:
$$p_p = K_p \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 3.0219 \times 21 \times 6 = \mathbf{380.76\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
(inclined at β = 10° to horizontal).
Q.1 (b) ii 2025 3M Numerical 4x
A rough vertical wall of 7.5 m height supports a horizontal backfill. If the angle of internal friction and angle of wall friction are respectively 33° and 12°, compute the passive earth pressure at the bottom of wall. Assume density of 18.5 kN/m³.
Given Parameters:
Height H = 7.5 m, φ = 33°, δ = 12°, γ = 18.5 kN/m³, vertical wall (α = 90°), horizontal backfill (β = 0°).
1.
Coulomb's Passive Earth Pressure Coefficient (Kp): For vertical wall with horizontal backfill:
$$K_p = \frac{\cos^2\phi}{\cos\delta \left[1 - \sqrt{\frac{\sin(\phi + \delta)\sin\phi}{\cos\delta}}\right]^2}$$
2.
Trigonometric Values:
$$\cos 33^\circ = 0.8387 \implies \cos^2 33^\circ = 0.7034$$

$$\cos 12^\circ = 0.9781$$

$$\sin(\phi + \delta) = \sin 45^\circ = 0.7071$$

$$\sin 33^\circ = 0.5446$$

$$\sqrt{\frac{0.7071 \times 0.5446}{0.9781}} = \sqrt{\frac{0.3851}{0.9781}} = \sqrt{0.3937} = 0.6275$$

$$\left[1 - 0.6275\right]^2 = 0.3725^2 = 0.1388$$

$$K_p = \frac{0.7034}{0.9781 \times 0.1388} = \frac{0.7034}{0.1358} = \mathbf{5.180}$$
3.
Passive Earth Pressure at Bottom of Wall (z = 7.5 m):
$$p_p = K_p \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 5.180 \times 18.5 \times 7.5 = \mathbf{718.73\text{ kN/m}^2}$$

Acts at an angle δ = 12° upwards to the normal.
Q.1 (b) iii 2025 3M Numerical 2x
A retaining wall of 4.5 m height carries a horizontal backfill with c = 35 kN/m², φ = 10°; γ = 17.2 kN/m³. The water table is located at 1.50 m below the ground. Sketch the distribution of active earth pressure. Assume the value of angle of internal friction is 14°; and cohesion c = 50 kN/m² in the submerged condition.
Given Parameters:
Total height H = 4.5 m. Water table at depth H1 = 1.5 m below ground. Submerged stratum H2 = 3.0 m.
Layer 1 (0 to 1.5 m): c1 = 35 kN/m², φ1 = 10°, γ1 = 17.2 kN/m³.
Layer 2 (1.5 to 4.5 m): c2 = 50 kN/m², φ2 = 14°, γsat = 20 kN/m³ (γ' = 20 - 9.81 = 10.19 kN/m³).
1.
Active Earth Pressure Coefficients:
$$K_{a1} = \frac{1 - \sin 10^\circ}{1 + \sin 10^\circ} = \frac{1 - 0.1736}{1 + 0.1736} = 0.7041 \implies \sqrt{K_{a1}} = 0.8391$$

$$K_{a2} = \frac{1 - \sin 14^\circ}{1 + \sin 14^\circ} = \frac{1 - 0.2419}{1 + 0.2419} = 0.6104 \implies \sqrt{K_{a2}} = 0.7813$$
2. Pressure Distribution by Depths:
•
At Ground Surface (z = 0 m):
$$\sigma'_v = 0 \implies p_{a0} = 0 - 2 c_1 \sqrt{K_{a1}} = -2 \times 35 \times 0.8391 = \mathbf{-58.74\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
(Tensile crack zone).
•
At Top Layer Interface (z = 1.5 m, above WT):
$$\sigma'_v = 17.2 \times 1.5 = 25.8\text{ kPa} \implies p_{a1} = 25.8(0.7041) - 58.74 = 18.17 - 58.74 = \mathbf{-40.57\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
•
At Bottom Layer Interface (z = 1.5 m, below WT):
$$\sigma'_v = 25.8\text{ kPa} \implies p_{a1}' = 25.8(0.6104) - 2(50)(0.7813) = 15.75 - 78.13 = \mathbf{-62.38\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
•
At Base of Wall (z = 4.5 m):
$$\sigma'_v = 25.8 + 10.19 \times 3.0 = 56.37\text{ kPa}$$

$$p_{a,soil} = 56.37(0.6104) - 78.13 = 34.41 - 78.13 = -43.72\text{ kN/m}^2 \approx 0$$
(cohesion suppresses effective thrust).
•
Hydrostatic Water Pressure at Base:
$$u = \gamma_w \times H_2 = 9.81 \times 3.0 = \mathbf{29.43\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
3.
Net Pressure Distribution: Tensile stresses exist throughout the soil depth due to high cohesion (c = 35 to 50 kPa). When tension cracks are ignored or braced, the net lateral pressure acting on the wall consists predominantly of hydrostatic water pressure u = 29.43 kN/m² at the base.
Q.1 (c) 2025 6M Derivation 2x
Derive the condition of maximum active earth pressure from sliding wedge.
Derivation of Condition for Maximum Active Earth Pressure (Sliding Wedge Method):
1.
Equilibrium of Trial Wedge (ABC): Consider a planar failure wedge with failure surface inclined at angle θ to the horizontal. The forces in equilibrium are:
•
W: Weight of sliding wedge ABC =
$$\frac{1}{2}\gamma H \cdot BC = \frac{1}{2}\gamma H^2 \frac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \theta)}{\sin^2\alpha \sin(\theta - \beta)}$$
.
•
R: Soil reaction across failure surface inclined at φ to the normal.
•
Pa: Active thrust on wall face inclined at δ to normal.
2.
Applying Sine Rule to Force Triangle: From the closed polygon of forces (W, R, Pa):
$$\frac{P_a}{\sin(\theta - \phi)} = \frac{W}{\sin(180^\circ - (\alpha + \theta - \phi + \delta))}$$

$$P_a = W \cdot \frac{\sin(\theta - \phi)}{\sin(\alpha + \theta - \phi + \delta)}$$
3.
Condition for Maximum Thrust: To find the critical failure plane that delivers the maximum lateral active thrust, set the partial derivative with respect to θ to zero:
$$\frac{\partial P_a}{\partial \theta} = 0$$

Differentiating using quotient rule yields the classical Coulomb wedge condition:
$$\frac{\partial W}{\partial \theta} \sin(\alpha + \theta - \phi + \delta) - W \cos(\alpha + \theta - \phi + \delta) = 0$$
4.
Resulting Coulomb Active Thrust Equation: Solving for critical wedge angle θcr gives the maximum active thrust:
$$P_a = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 K_a$$

Where Coulomb's active coefficient is:
$$K_a = \frac{\sin^2(\alpha + \phi)}{\sin^2\alpha \sin(\alpha - \delta) \left[1 + \sqrt{\frac{\sin(\phi + \delta)\sin(\phi - \beta)}{\sin(\alpha - \delta)\sin(\alpha + \beta)}}\right]^2}$$
.
Q.1 (c) OR 2025 6M Theory / Derivation 3x
Explain the Rebhann's graphical construction for active earth pressure and prove that it satisfy the condition of maximum earth pressure
Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Earth Thrust:
Based on Poncelet's modification of Coulomb's wedge theory for determining maximum active thrust graphically.
1. Construction Procedure:
•
Draw backfill surface AD and wall back AB inclined at α to horizontal.
•
Draw φ-line BD from the heel B inclined at angle φ to horizontal, meeting ground surface at D.
•
Draw ψ-line BL from heel B inclined at angle ψ = (α - δ) to BD.
•
Draw semi-circle on BD as diameter.
•
From wall top A, draw line AE parallel to ψ-line BL, meeting BD at E.
•
Erect perpendicular EF at E to intersect semi-circle at F.
•
With center B and radius BF, draw arc cutting BD at point T.
•
Through T, draw line TC parallel to ψ-line BL, intersecting ground surface at C. Line BC defines the critical failure surface.
•
Through T, draw line TP parallel to AE to cut BC at P.
2.
Magnitude of Total Active Thrust:
$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area of } \Delta CPT$$
3. Mathematical Proof of Maximum Earth Thrust:
•
The active thrust from a sliding wedge ABC is
$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area}(\Delta ABC) \cdot \frac{\sin(\theta - \phi)}{\sin(\alpha + \theta - \phi + \delta)}$$
.
•
By geometric similarity of triangles ΔBDC and ΔCPT:
$$\text{Area}(\Delta CPT) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot CT \cdot PT \cdot \sin\psi$$
•
For maximum thrust:
$$\frac{\partial P_a}{\partial \theta} = 0 \iff BT^2 = BD \cdot BE$$
.
•
Since BF is the mean proportional in semi-circle BFD on diameter BD:
$$BF^2 = BD \cdot BE$$
.
•
But radius BT = BF, therefore
$$BT^2 = BD \cdot BE$$
holds identically.
•
Hence, Rebhann's graphical construction strictly satisfies the condition of maximum active earth pressure.
Unit 2 Shear Strength & Slope Stability 0/7
Q.2 (b) i 2025 3M Theory 3x
Describe the three modes of shear failure in soil. Draw load-settlement curves for each mode and explain which type of soil exhibits each failure pattern.
Three Modes of Shear Failure in Soil (Vesic):
1. General Shear Failure:
•
Continuous, well-defined slip surfaces extend from footing edges to the ground surface.
•
Significant soil bulging/heaving occurs adjacent to the foundation, accompanied by sudden catastrophic tilting.
•
Load-settlement curve shows a clear, distinct peak failure load.
•
Soil Type: Dense sand (Dr > 70%, φ > 36°) and stiff, overconsolidated clays under shallow footings.
2. Local Shear Failure:
•
Shear failure planes develop clearly beneath the footing but terminate within the soil mass without extending to the surface.
•
Only slight bulging occurs with noticeable continuous settlement.
•
Load-settlement curve has no clear peak; ultimate load is taken where settlement rate increases steeply.
•
Soil Type: Medium dense sand (35% < Dr < 70%, 28° ≤ φ ≤ 36°) and medium-consistency clays.
3. Punching Shear Failure:
•
Failure pattern consists of vertical downward compression directly beneath the footing wedge.
•
Zero bulging or heaving at ground surface; soil outside remains unaffected.
•
Load-settlement curve shows steep continuous plunging settlement with no definite yield point.
•
Soil Type: Very loose sand (Dr < 35%, φ < 28°), soft sensitive clays, and deep footings.
Q.3 (a) 2025 2M Theory 2x
Discuss Coulomb's law of shear strength of soil
Coulomb's Law of Shear Strength of Soil:
States that the shear strength (τf) along any failure plane within a soil mass is governed by internal cohesion and frictional resistance directly proportional to the normal stress.
1.
Total Stress Formulation:
$$\tau_f = c + \sigma \tan\phi$$
2.
Terzaghi's Effective Stress Formulation (Modern Form):
$$\tau_f = c' + \sigma' \tan\phi' = c' + (\sigma - u) \tan\phi'$$
3. Parameter Definitions:
•
c / c': Cohesion intercept (cementation and intermolecular bonds) in kPa.
•
σ / σ': Total and effective normal stress acting on the failure plane in kPa.
•
φ / φ': Angle of shearing resistance (interparticle friction and interlocking).
•
u: Pore water pressure in kPa.
Example: Pure sand has c' = 0, giving τf = σ' tan φ'; pure saturated clay under undrained condition has φu = 0, giving τf = cu.
Q.3 (b) i 2025 3M Numerical 2x
The shear stress and normal stress at a failure plane in a cohesionless soil mass were found to be 4 kPa and 10 kPa respectively. Determine the resultant stress on failure plane and inclination of failure plane. Also compute the shear parameters.
Given Parameters:
Shear stress on failure plane τ = 4 kPa, normal stress σ = 10 kPa, cohesionless soil (c = 0).
1.
Resultant Stress on Failure Plane (R):
$$R = \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \tau^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{116} = \mathbf{10.77\text{ kPa}}$$
2.
Shear Parameter (Angle of Internal Friction φ): For cohesionless soil (c = 0), the failure envelope passes through the origin:
$$\tau = \sigma \tan\phi \implies \tan\phi = \frac{\tau}{\sigma} = \frac{4}{10} = 0.40$$

$$\phi = \tan^{-1}(0.40) = \mathbf{21.80^\circ}, \quad c = 0$$
3.
Inclination of Failure Plane (θcr): The critical failure plane is inclined at θcr to the major principal plane:
$$\theta_{cr} = 45^\circ + \frac{\phi}{2} = 45^\circ + \frac{21.80^\circ}{2} = \mathbf{55.90^\circ}$$

Angle of obliquity on the failure plane is ψ = φ = 21.80°.
Q.3 (b) ii 2025 3M Numerical 2x
The deviator force to shear the soil specimen of 38 mm diameter and 76 mm height under a confining pressure of 100 kN/m² is 251 N while it shears under a deviator force of 327 N at a confining pressure of 200 kN/m². The deformation at the time of failure is respectively 2.0 mm and 5.2 mm. Determine the shear parameters. Determine the deviator stress under confining pressure of 250 kPa.
Given Parameters:
d0 = 38 mm = 0.038 m, L0 = 76 mm = 0.076 m.
Initial area:
$$A_0 = \frac{\pi}{4}(0.038)^2 = 1.134 \times 10^{-3} m^2 = 1134\text{ mm}^2$$
.
1.
Test 1 (σ3 = 100 kPa): Deformation ΔL1 = 2.0 mm → axial strain
$$\epsilon_1 = \frac{2.0}{76} = 0.0263$$
.
Corrected area:
$$A_{c1} = \frac{A_0}{1 - \epsilon_1} = \frac{1.134 \times 10^{-3}}{1 - 0.0263} = 1.165 \times 10^{-3} m^2$$
.
Deviator stress:
$$\sigma_{d1} = \frac{P_1}{A_{c1}} = \frac{251 \times 10^{-3} kN}{1.165 \times 10^{-3} m^2} = \mathbf{215.45\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Major principal stress:
$$\sigma_1 = 100 + 215.45 = \mathbf{315.45\text{ kPa}}$$
.
2.
Test 2 (σ3 = 200 kPa): Deformation ΔL2 = 5.2 mm → axial strain
$$\epsilon_2 = \frac{5.2}{76} = 0.0684$$
.
Corrected area:
$$A_{c2} = \frac{1.134 \times 10^{-3}}{1 - 0.0684} = 1.217 \times 10^{-3} m^2$$
.
Deviator stress:
$$\sigma_{d2} = \frac{327 \times 10^{-3}}{1.217 \times 10^{-3}} = \mathbf{268.69\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Major principal stress:
$$\sigma_1 = 200 + 268.69 = \mathbf{468.69\text{ kPa}}$$
.
3.
Mohr-Coulomb Failure Equation:
$$\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 N_\phi + 2 c \sqrt{N_\phi}$$

Subtracting Test 1 from Test 2:
$$468.69 - 315.45 = N_\phi(200 - 100) \implies 153.24 = 100 N_\phi \implies N_\phi = \mathbf{1.5324}$$
.
Angle of friction:
$$\frac{1 + \sin\phi}{1 - \sin\phi} = 1.5324 \implies \sin\phi = \frac{0.5324}{2.5324} = 0.2102 \implies \phi = \mathbf{12.13^\circ}$$
.
Cohesion intercept:
$$315.45 = 100(1.5324) + 2 c \sqrt{1.5324} \implies 2 c (1.2379) = 162.21 \implies c = \mathbf{65.52\text{ kPa}}$$
.
4.
Deviator Stress at Confining Pressure σ3 = 250 kPa:
$$\sigma_1 = 250(1.5324) + 2(65.52)(1.2379) = 383.10 + 162.21 = 545.31\text{ kPa}$$

$$\sigma_d = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3 = 545.31 - 250 = \mathbf{295.31\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Q.3 (b) iii 2025 3M Theory 4x
Explain various kinds of triaxial tests. Which test is best suited for the cohesive soil deposit having a permeable layer immediately below the foundation level?
1. Three Kinds of Triaxial Shear Tests:
1.
Unconsolidated Undrained (UU / Quick Test): Zero drainage allowed during both cell pressure application and shear stage. Measures undrained shear strength (cu, φu = 0 for saturated soil). Appropriate for short-term end-of-construction stability.
2.
Consolidated Undrained (CU Test): Complete drainage permitted under cell pressure until consolidation completes; shear stage is undrained with pore water pressure measurement. Gives effective parameters (c', φ') and undrained parameters.
3.
Consolidated Drained (CD / Slow Test): Full drainage allowed during cell pressure consolidation and during shearing at an extremely slow strain rate so pore pressure remains zero (Δu = 0). Measures true drained effective parameters (c', φ').
2. Test Selection for Cohesive Deposit with Permeable Layer Below Foundation:
•
Best Suited Test: Consolidated Drained (CD) Test or Consolidated Undrained (CU) Test with pore pressure measurement.
•
Engineering Justification: The presence of an immediately adjacent permeable layer provides a short drainage boundary path, allowing water to dissipate rapidly during and after construction. A CD or CU test accurately reproduces this field dissipation mechanism, providing the true drained effective shear parameters required for long-term bearing capacity and stability analysis.
Q.3 (c) 2025 6M Derivation 2x
Derive a relationship between effective shear parameters and principal stresses.
Derivation of Relationship Between Effective Shear Parameters (c', φ') and Principal Stresses (σ'1, σ'3):
1.
Geometry of Mohr Circle at Failure: Consider a soil element subjected to effective principal stresses σ'1 and σ'3. The Mohr circle is tangent to the failure envelope τf = c' + σ' tan φ' at failure point F.
•
Center of circle:
$$C = \left(\frac{\sigma'_1 + \sigma'_3}{2}, 0\right)$$
•
Radius of circle:
$$R = CF = \frac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}$$
•
Origin of failure line:
$$O' = (-c' \cot\phi', 0)$$
2.
Formulating Trigonometric Relation in ΔO'CF: Triangle O'CF is right-angled at F (∠O'FC = 90°):
$$\sin\phi' = \frac{CF}{O'C} = \frac{\frac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}}{\frac{\sigma'_1 + \sigma'_3}{2} + c'\cot\phi'}$$

Cross-multiplying:
$$\left(\frac{\sigma'_1 + \sigma'_3}{2} + c'\frac{\cos\phi'}{\sin\phi'}\right) \sin\phi' = \frac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}$$

$$\left(\frac{\sigma'_1 + \sigma'_3}{2}\right)\sin\phi' + c'\cos\phi' = \frac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}$$
3.
Regrouping σ'1 and σ'3 Terms:
$$\frac{\sigma'_1}{2}(1 - \sin\phi') = \frac{\sigma'_3}{2}(1 + \sin\phi') + c'\cos\phi'$$

Dividing through by
$$\frac{1 - \sin\phi'}{2}$$
:
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 \left(\frac{1 + \sin\phi'}{1 - \sin\phi'}\right) + 2 c' \frac{\cos\phi'}{1 - \sin\phi'}$$
4.
Trigonometric Simplifications:
$$\frac{1 + \sin\phi'}{1 - \sin\phi'} = \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) = N_\phi$$

$$\frac{\cos\phi'}{1 - \sin\phi'} = \frac{\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\phi'}}{1 - \sin\phi'} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin\phi'}{1 - \sin\phi'}} = \tan\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) = \sqrt{N_\phi}$$
5.
Final Governing Equation:
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 N_\phi + 2 c' \sqrt{N_\phi} = \sigma'_3 \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) + 2 c' \tan\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right)$$
.
Q.3 (c) OR 2025 6M Numerical 2x
The following data refers to a triaxial compression tests performed on a soil sample. Determine the total and effective shear parameters of soil.
Observation 1: σ3 = 80 kPa, σd = 175 kPa, u = 45 kPa
Observation 2: σ3 = 150 kPa, σd = 240 kPa, u = 50 kPa
Observation 3: σ3 = 210 kPa, σd = 300 kPa, u = 60 kPa
Stress Computations Table:
•
Obs 1: σ3 = 80 kPa, σ1 = 80 + 175 = 255 kPa; σ'3 = 80 - 45 = 35 kPa, σ'1 = 255 - 45 = 210 kPa.
•
Obs 2: σ3 = 150 kPa, σ1 = 150 + 240 = 390 kPa; σ'3 = 150 - 50 = 100 kPa, σ'1 = 390 - 50 = 340 kPa.
•
Obs 3: σ3 = 210 kPa, σ1 = 210 + 300 = 510 kPa; σ'3 = 210 - 60 = 150 kPa, σ'1 = 510 - 60 = 450 kPa.
1.
Total Shear Parameters (c, φ): Using observations 1 and 3:
$$\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 N_\phi + 2 c \sqrt{N_\phi}$$

$$510 - 255 = N_\phi(210 - 80) \implies 255 = 130 N_\phi \implies N_\phi = 1.9615$$

$$\sin\phi = \frac{N_\phi - 1}{N_\phi + 1} = \frac{0.9615}{2.9615} = 0.3247 \implies \phi = \mathbf{18.95^\circ}$$

$$255 = 80(1.9615) + 2 c \sqrt{1.9615} \implies 2 c (1.4005) = 255 - 156.92 = 98.08 \implies c = \mathbf{35.01\text{ kPa}}$$
.
2.
Effective Shear Parameters (c', φ'): Using effective stresses for observations 1 and 3:
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 N'_\phi + 2 c' \sqrt{N'_\phi}$$

$$450 - 210 = N'_\phi(150 - 35) \implies 240 = 115 N'_\phi \implies N'_\phi = 2.0870$$

$$\sin\phi' = \frac{N'_\phi - 1}{N'_\phi + 1} = \frac{1.0870}{3.0870} = 0.3521 \implies \phi' = \mathbf{20.62^\circ}$$

$$210 = 35(2.0870) + 2 c' \sqrt{2.0870} \implies 2 c' (1.4446) = 210 - 73.05 = 136.95 \implies c' = \mathbf{47.40\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Final Summary:
•
Total parameters: c = 35.0 kPa, φ = 19.0°.
•
Effective parameters: c' = 47.4 kPa, φ' = 20.6°.
Unit 3 Shallow Foundations 0/10
Q.2 (a) 2025 2M Theory 2x
What do you mean by bearing capacity? What are the different suffixes to be used before bearing capacity?
1.
Bearing Capacity of Soil: The maximum load-carrying resistance per unit area that the underlying soil or rock mass can support without undergoing shear failure or excessive foundation settlement.
Example: A footing imposing a contact pressure of 200 kPa on soil capable of resisting 500 kPa without failure.
2. Different Suffixes Used Before Bearing Capacity:
1.
Gross Ultimate (qu / qult): Total intensity of loading at base of foundation at which soil fails in shear.
2.
Net Ultimate (qnu): Ultimate intensity above initial effective surcharge:
$$q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f$$
.
3.
Net Safe (qns): Net ultimate capacity divided by factor of safety:
$$q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{FOS}$$
.
4.
Gross Safe (qs): Maximum gross intensity safe against shear failure:
$$q_s = q_{ns} + \gamma D_f = \frac{q_{nu}}{FOS} + \gamma D_f$$
.
5.
Safe Bearing Pressure (qps): Maximum allowable net intensity that limits total and differential settlement to tolerable values (e.g. ≤ 25 mm).
6.
Allowable Bearing Capacity (qa): Final design value; smaller of gross safe (qs) and safe bearing pressure (qps).
Q.2 (b) ii 2025 3M Theory 3x
Explain the effect of water table on bearing capacity of soils.
Effect of Water Table on Bearing Capacity:
Submergence halves the effective unit weight of soil (γ' ≈ 0.5 γbulk), thereby reducing effective overburden stress and shear resistance.
1.
Governing Terzaghi Equation with Correction Factors:
$$q_{ult} = c N_c + \gamma D_f N_q \cdot R_{w1} + 0.5 \gamma B N_\gamma \cdot R_{w2}$$
2.
Water Table Correction Factor Rw1 (Surcharge Zone): Applies to soil above footing base (depth zw1 from ground surface, 0 ≤ zw1 ≤ Df):
$$R_{w1} = 0.5 \left(1 + \frac{z_{w1}}{D_f}\right)$$
•
If WT is at ground level (zw1 = 0): Rw1 = 0.5 (50% reduction in surcharge term).
•
If WT is at or below footing base (zw1 = Df): Rw1 = 1.0 (no reduction).
3.
Water Table Correction Factor Rw2 (Wedge Zone): Applies to soil within wedge depth B below base (depth zw2 from base, 0 ≤ zw2 ≤ B):
$$R_{w2} = 0.5 \left(1 + \frac{z_{w2}}{B}\right)$$
•
If WT is at foundation base (zw2 = 0): Rw2 = 0.5 (50% reduction in soil weight term).
•
If WT is at depth ≥ B below base (zw2 ≥ B): Rw2 = 1.0 (zero effect on bearing capacity).
4.
Engineering Significance: Rise of water table to ground level causes an overall 50% reduction in the ultimate bearing capacity of cohesionless soils.
Q.2 (b) iii 2025 3M Numerical 2x
Compute the net safe bearing capacity of a square footing of size 2.5 m, provided at 2.0 m depth in a purely cohesive soil with Unconfined Shear Strength of 150 kN/m² and density being 18 kN/m³. Use factor of safety as 2.5.
Given Parameters:
Footing size B = 2.5 m, depth Df = 2.0 m, γ = 18 kN/m³, unconfined compressive strength qu = 150 kN/m², FOS = 2.5, purely cohesive soil (φ = 0).
1.
Cohesion Intercept (cu):
$$c_u = \frac{q_u}{2} = \frac{150}{2} = \mathbf{75\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
2.
Terzaghi Bearing Capacity Factors for φ = 0:
$$N_c = 5.7, \quad N_q = 1.0, \quad N_\gamma = 0$$

For square footing, shape factor sc = 1.3:
3.
Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (qnu):
$$q_{nu} = 1.3 c_u N_c = 1.3 \times 75 \times 5.7 = \mathbf{555.75\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
4.
Net Safe Bearing Capacity (qns):
$$q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{FOS} = \frac{555.75}{2.5} = \mathbf{222.30\text{ kN/m}^2}$$

Note: Depth Df and soil density γ do not affect net ultimate/safe capacity in pure clay (φ = 0).
Q.2 (c) 2025 6M Numerical 4x
A square footing of 3.5 m is resting at 3 m below the ground level. The shear parameters of soil are respectively 40 kN/m² and 12°. The density of soil is 20 kN/m³. The water table lies at 2 m below the base of footing. Calculate the net safe bearing capacity. Assume factor of safety of 3.0.
Given Parameters:
Square footing B = 3.5 m, Df = 3.0 m, c = 40 kN/m², φ = 12°, γ = 20 kN/m³, WT depth below base zw2 = 2.0 m, FOS = 3.0.
Since φ = 12° < 28°, local shear failure governs.
1.
Mobilized Shear Parameters:
$$c_m = \frac{2}{3} c = \frac{2}{3} \times 40 = 26.67\text{ kN/m}^2$$

$$\tan\phi_m = \frac{2}{3}\tan 12^\circ = \frac{2}{3}(0.2126) = 0.1417 \implies \phi_m \approx 8.06^\circ$$
2.
Bearing Capacity Factors (Table 1 / IS: 6403 for φm ≈ 8.1°): Interpolating between φ = 5° and 10° (Table 1: φ=10° → N_c=5.14, N_q=1.00, N_γ=0.00):
$$N'_c \approx 7.0, \quad N'_q \approx 1.8, \quad N'_\gamma \approx 0.4$$
3.
Water Table Correction Factor (zw2 = 2.0 m < B = 3.5 m): Water table is below footing base, so Rw1 = 1.0 (surcharge is dry).
$$R_{w2} = 0.5 \left(1 + \frac{z_{w2}}{B}\right) = 0.5 \left(1 + \frac{2.0}{3.5}\right) = 0.5(1 + 0.5714) = \mathbf{0.7857}$$
4.
Terzaghi Net Ultimate Capacity for Square Footing:
$$q_{nu} = 1.3 c_m N'_c + \gamma D_f (N'_q - 1) + 0.4 \gamma B N'_\gamma \cdot R_{w2}$$

$$= 1.3(26.67)(7.0) + 20(3.0)(1.8 - 1) + 0.4(20)(3.5)(0.4)(0.7857)$$

$$= 242.70 + 48.00 + 8.80 = \mathbf{299.50\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
5.
Net Safe Bearing Capacity:
$$q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{FOS} = \frac{299.50}{3.0} = \mathbf{99.83\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Q.2 (c) OR 2025 6M Numerical 2x
A rectangular footing 3 m x 2 m carries a load of 1500 kN with eccentricity of 0.3 m along the length and 0.2 m along the width. The footing is located at 1.5 m depth in soil with c = 20 kN/m², φ = 25°, γ = 19 kN/m³. Calculate the maximum pressure at the base and check for safety.
Given Parameters:
L = 3.0 m, B = 2.0 m, Q = 1500 kN, eL = 0.3 m, eB = 0.2 m, Df = 1.5 m, c = 20 kN/m², φ = 25°, γ = 19 kN/m³.
1.
Eccentricity Limit Check (Kern of Section):
$$\frac{e_L}{L} = \frac{0.3}{3.0} = 0.10 \le \frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167 \quad \text{(Safe, zero tension)}$$

$$\frac{e_B}{B} = \frac{0.2}{2.0} = 0.10 \le \frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167 \quad \text{(Safe, zero tension)}$$
2.
Maximum Base Pressure (Elastic Distribution):
$$q_{max} = \frac{Q}{B L} \left(1 + \frac{6 e_L}{L} + \frac{6 e_B}{B}\right)$$

$$q_{max} = \frac{1500}{2.0 \times 3.0} \left(1 + \frac{6 \times 0.3}{3.0} + \frac{6 \times 0.2}{2.0}\right) = 250 \left(1 + 0.60 + 0.60\right) = 250(2.20) = \mathbf{550.0\text{ kN/m}^2}$$

$$q_{min} = \frac{Q}{BL}\left(1 - \frac{6 e_L}{L} - \frac{6 e_B}{B}\right) = 250(1 - 1.20) = -50\text{ kN/m}^2$$
(slight separation at extreme corner).
3.
Meyerhof's Effective Dimensions for Bearing Capacity:
$$L' = L - 2 e_L = 3.0 - 2(0.3) = 2.4\text{ m}$$

$$B' = B - 2 e_B = 2.0 - 2(0.2) = 1.6\text{ m}$$

From Table 1 for φ = 25°: Nc = 10.98, Nq = 3.94, Nγ = 2.65.
$$q_{ult} = c N_c \left(1 + 0.2\frac{B'}{L'}\right) + \gamma D_f N_q + 0.5 \gamma B' N_\gamma \left(1 - 0.2\frac{B'}{L'}\right)$$

$$= 20(10.98)(1 + 0.2\frac{1.6}{2.4}) + 19(1.5)(3.94) + 0.5(19)(1.6)(2.65)(1 - 0.2\frac{1.6}{2.4})$$

$$= 20(10.98)(1.133) + 112.29 + 40.28(0.867) = 248.81 + 112.29 + 34.92 = \mathbf{396.02\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
4.
Safety Check: Average effective pressure:
$$q'_{avg} = \frac{Q}{B' L'} = \frac{1500}{1.6 \times 2.4} = 390.63\text{ kN/m}^2 \approx q_{ult}$$
.
$$FOS = \frac{q_{ult}}{q'_{avg}} = \frac{396.02}{390.63} = \mathbf{1.01 < 2.5}$$
.
Conclusion: UNSAFE in shear; footing dimensions must be increased or eccentricity reduced.
Q.4 (a) 2025 2M Theory 2x
What are different types of shallow foundations? Draw neat sketch of strap footing.
1. Types of Shallow Foundations (Df ≤ B):
1.
Isolated / Spread Footing: Individual pad supporting a single column.
2.
Strip / Wall Footing: Continuous concrete strip supporting a load-bearing wall or row of closely spaced columns.
3.
Combined Footing: Common base slab supporting two columns (rectangular or trapezoidal when column loads differ).
4.
Strap / Cantilever Footing: Two isolated footings joined by a stiff cantilever beam that does not touch the soil.
5.
Raft / Mat Foundation: Large continuous slab supporting all columns and walls over the entire building footprint.
2. Strap Footing Sketch & Features:
•
Used when an exterior column is located at the property boundary line and cannot project outward.
•
A rigid strap beam connects the exterior footing to an adjacent interior footing.
•
The strap beam is isolated from soil beneath it (zero soil pressure under beam), transferring overturning moment to the interior footing without causing eccentricity on the soil.
Q.4 (b) i 2025 3M Theory 3x
Enumerate the requirements of satisfactory foundations.
Four Fundamental Requirements of a Satisfactory Foundation:
1.
Shear Failure / Bearing Capacity Criterion: The foundation must have an adequate factor of safety (minimum FOS ≥ 2.5 to 3.0) against ultimate shear failure of the supporting soil mass under all severe design load combinations.
2.
Settlement Criterion: Total settlement and differential settlement between adjacent columns must remain strictly within permissible limits (IS: 1904: isolated footings ≤ 50 mm in clay, ≤ 25 mm in sand; differential ≤ 1/500) to prevent cracking or structural distress.
3.
Location & Depth Criterion: Must be placed below the depth of topsoil, frost penetration zone, seasonal volume change/shrinkage depth in expansive clays, and maximum scour depth in riverine foundations.
4.
Stability & Durability Criterion: Must resist lateral sliding, overturning moments, and hydrostatic uplift; foundation concrete and reinforcement must be durable against sulfate and chloride ground attack.
Q.4 (b) ii 2025 3M Theory 2x
Two buildings are to be constructed at two different sites. First site shows the low compressive cohesive soil profile up to 10 m depth followed by good quality rock up to 15 m depth below the ground while the second site is having expansive soil up to 5 m depth followed by good rock up to 10 m below the ground. G+4 story building is to be constructed at the first site while at the second site G+15 story building is to be constructed. Suggest the type of foundation at two different sites for the structures to be constructed.
1. Foundation Selection for Site 1 (G+4 Building on Soft Clay):
•
Subsoil Profile: Low compressive strength cohesive soil (soft clay) up to 10 m depth, underlain by good quality rock extending to 15 m.
•
Structure: Medium-load 5-story frame (G+4).
•
Recommended Foundation: End-Bearing Driven Cast-in-Situ or Bored Concrete Piles (diameter 400-500 mm) terminating and socketed 1-2 m into the sound rock stratum at 10 m depth.
•
Alternative: Under-reamed piles if loads are modest, or a compensated raft foundation if settlement analysis allows.
2. Foundation Selection for Site 2 (G+15 Building on Expansive Soil over Rock):
•
Subsoil Profile: Highly expansive soil (black cotton clay) up to 5 m depth (active zone of severe seasonal heave/shrinkage), underlain by stable ground and sound rock at 10 m depth.
•
Structure: Heavy high-rise 16-story tower (G+15) with substantial column loads, moments, and wind shear.
•
Recommended Foundation: Large-Diameter Bored Cast-in-Situ Piles (Drilled Shafts / Piers) Socketed into Sound Rock at 10 m depth.
•
Special Protection: Provide sacrificial casing or low-friction bituminous coating through the top 5 m expansive zone to eliminate uplifting drag forces (negative skin friction during swelling) on the pile shaft.
Q.4 (b) iii 2025 3M Numerical 2x
Using the soil properties (γ = 17.5 kN/m³, c = 20 kN/m², φ = 20°), and assuming the square footing (3.415 m x 3.415 m) located at a depth of 1.5 m carries a total load of 2000 kN. Calculate the immediate settlement of the footing using the elastic theory. Assume the soil is homogeneous and isotropic with a Poisson's ratio of 0.3 and Young's modulus of 50,000 kN/m². (assume influence factor 0.88 for square footing)
Given Parameters:
B = L = 3.415 m, Df = 1.5 m, Q = 2000 kN, μ = 0.3, Es = 50,000 kN/m², If = 0.88.
1.
Contact Pressure (q):
$$q = \frac{Q}{B \times L} = \frac{2000}{3.415 \times 3.415} = \frac{2000}{11.6622} = \mathbf{171.49\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
2.
Schleicher's Elastic Theory Equation: Immediate elastic settlement of a flexible footing:
$$S_i = \frac{q B (1 - \mu^2)}{E_s} \cdot I_f$$
3.
Step-by-Step Substitution:
$$1 - \mu^2 = 1 - (0.3)^2 = 1 - 0.09 = 0.91$$

$$S_i = \frac{171.49 \times 3.415 \times 0.91}{50000} \times 0.88$$

$$S_i = \frac{532.93}{50000} \times 0.88 = 0.01066 \times 0.88 = \mathbf{0.00938\text{ m} = 9.38\text{ mm}}$$
Result: Immediate settlement Si = 9.38 mm (≤ permissible 25 mm).
Q.4 (c) OR 2025 6M Numerical 2x
Design a strip footing resting at 2.0 m below the ground and to carrying a load of 1000 kN/m, the shear parameters c = 50 kN/m² and angle of internal friction is 22° while the density of soil is 20 kN/m³. The factor of safety to be used is 2.5.
Given Parameters:
Df = 2.0 m, line load P = 1000 kN/m, c = 50 kN/m², φ = 22°, γ = 20 kN/m³, FOS = 2.5.
Since φ = 22° < 28°, local shear failure governs.
1.
Mobilized Shear Parameters:
$$c_m = \frac{2}{3} c = \frac{2}{3}(50) = 33.33\text{ kN/m}^2$$

$$\tan\phi_m = \frac{2}{3}\tan 22^\circ = \frac{2}{3}(0.4040) = 0.2693 \implies \phi_m \approx 15.07^\circ$$
2.
Bearing Capacity Factors (Table 1 for φ ≈ 15°):
$$N'_c = 6.49, \quad N'_q = 1.57, \quad N'_\gamma = 0.45$$
3.
Terzaghi Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity for Strip Footing:
$$q_{nu} = c_m N'_c + \gamma D_f (N'_q - 1) + 0.5 \gamma B N'_\gamma$$

$$q_{nu} = 33.33(6.49) + 20(2.0)(1.57 - 1) + 0.5(20)(B)(0.45)$$

$$q_{nu} = 216.31 + 22.80 + 4.50 B = 239.11 + 4.50 B$$
4.
Equating Safe Capacity to Applied Stress:
$$q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{FOS} = \frac{239.11 + 4.50 B}{2.5} = 95.64 + 1.80 B$$

Applied net pressure from line load P:
$$q_{app} = \frac{P}{B} = \frac{1000}{B}$$

Setting qns = qapp:
$$95.64 + 1.80 B = \frac{1000}{B} \implies 1.80 B^2 + 95.64 B - 1000 = 0$$

Solving quadratic equation:
$$B = \frac{-95.64 + \sqrt{95.64^2 - 4(1.80)(-1000)}}{2(1.80)} = \frac{-95.64 + \sqrt{9147.0 + 7200}}{3.60} = \frac{-95.64 + 127.86}{3.60} = \frac{32.22}{3.60} = \mathbf{8.95\text{ m}}$$
.
5.
Design Specification: Provide strip footing of width B ≈ 9.0 m (or increase depth Df / provide pile foundation to reduce footing width).
Unit 4 Deep Foundations (Piles) 0/1
Q.4 (c) 2025 6M Numerical 2x
Design a square pile group to carry 500 kN load in clay with an unconfined compressive strength of 50 kN/m². Assume pile diameter of 400 mm and 6.0 m length. Adhesion factor may be taken as 0.6.
Given Parameters:
Working load Qw = 500 kN, qu = 50 kN/m², d = 0.4 m, L = 6.0 m, adhesion factor α = 0.6, FOS = 2.5.
1.
Undrained Cohesion of Clay:
$$c_u = \frac{q_u}{2} = \frac{50}{2} = \mathbf{25\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
2. Single Pile Ultimate Capacity (Qup):
•
End bearing:
$$Q_b = 9 c_u A_b = 9(25)\left[\frac{\pi}{4}(0.4)^2\right] = 225(0.1257) = \mathbf{28.28\text{ kN}}$$
.
•
Skin friction:
$$Q_s = \alpha c_u A_s = 0.6(25)[\pi(0.4)(6.0)] = 15(7.5398) = \mathbf{113.10\text{ kN}}$$
.
•
Total single pile:
$$Q_{up} = 28.28 + 113.10 = \mathbf{141.38\text{ kN}}$$
.
•
Safe load per pile:
$$Q_{safe} = \frac{Q_{up}}{FOS} = \frac{141.38}{2.5} = \mathbf{56.55\text{ kN}}$$
.
3.
Number of Piles Required (n):
$$n = \frac{Q_w}{Q_{safe}} = \frac{500}{56.55} = 8.84 \approx 9 \text{ piles}$$
.
Adopt a 3 × 3 square group (n = 9 piles), or a 4-pile group with larger spacing.
For a 3 × 3 group (n = 9):
Spacing s = 3d = 3(0.4) = 1.2 m center-to-center.
Group width:
$$B_g = 2s + d = 2(1.2) + 0.4 = \mathbf{2.8\text{ m}}$$
.
4. Block Failure Check (Qug):
•
Block base:
$$Q_{bg} = 9 c_u B_g^2 = 9(25)(2.8^2) = 225(7.84) = \mathbf{1764\text{ kN}}$$
.
•
Block perimeter:
$$Q_{sg} = 4 B_g L c_u = 4(2.8)(6.0)(25) = \mathbf{1680\text{ kN}}$$
.
•
Total block capacity:
$$Q_{ug} = 1764 + 1680 = \mathbf{3444\text{ kN}}$$
.
Safe block capacity:
$$\frac{3444}{2.5} = 1377.6\text{ kN} \gg 500\text{ kN} \quad \text{(Safe)}$$
.
5.
Group Efficiency:
$$\eta = \frac{Q_{ug}}{n \cdot Q_{up}} = \frac{3444}{9 \times 141.38} = \frac{3444}{1272.4} = 2.70 > 1.0 \implies \eta = 100\%$$
.
Group safe capacity is governed by individual action: 9 × 56.55 = 508.95 kN > 500 kN (Safe).
Unit 5 Soil Exploration & Testing 0/4
Q.5 (a) 2025 3M Theory 2x
Discuss different types of soil samples. How will you obtain undisturbed samples?
1. Three Types of Soil Samples:
1.
Non-Representative Disturbed Samples: Soil structure, moisture, and grain size distribution are all altered; mixture of soils from multiple strata (e.g. wash boring slurry, auger cuttings). Used only for preliminary identification.
2.
Representative Disturbed Samples: Soil natural structure is broken, but mineralogy, water content, and grain size distribution are fully preserved (e.g. split-spoon sampler). Used for classification, Atterberg limits, and specific gravity.
3.
Undisturbed Samples: Natural soil fabric, structure, density, void ratio, and moisture content are preserved with minimal disturbance. Essential for shear strength, consolidation, and permeability tests.
2. How to Obtain Undisturbed Samples:
•
Thin-Walled Sampler (Shelby Tube): Use seamless thin-walled steel tubes pushed steadily (never hammered) into soft-to-medium cohesive soils.
•
Area Ratio Criterion: Area ratio must be kept below 10%:
$$A_r = \frac{D_e^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2} \times 100\% \le 10\%$$
.
•
Clearance Ratios: Inside clearance Ci = 0.5% to 1.5% to reduce wall friction; outside clearance Co ≈ 0%.
•
Piston Sampler: For sensitive and soft saturated clays to prevent sample entry before sampling depth and provide vacuum suction during withdrawal.
•
Hand-Cut Block Samples: Carved directly from open test pits, wrapped in cheesecloth, and sealed with molten paraffin wax.
Q.5 (b) 2025 4M Theory 3x
What do you understand by geotechnical exploration? What are the different methods of subsoil explorations?
1.
Geotechnical Exploration: The systematic process of acquiring subsurface geological and soil engineering data across a project site to determine soil stratigraphy, ground water table elevation, engineering properties (shear strength, compressibility, permeability), and depth to bedrock for safe, economical foundation design.
2. Methods of Subsoil Exploration:
1.
Open Test Pits (Trial Pits): Shallow manual or backhoe excavation up to 3-5 m depth. Enables direct visual examination of soil strata and collection of pristine hand-carved undisturbed block samples.
2.
Auger Boring: Hand or power-driven helical/post-hole augers advancing in cohesive soils above the water table up to 10-15 m depth.
3.
Wash Boring: Water jet chopped inside casing pipe. Fast advancement in sands and soft clays; yields disturbed slurry samples.
4.
Rotary Core Drilling: Rapidly rotating diamond or tungsten core barrel with circulating drilling mud to core medium to hard rock and extract continuous rock cylinders for RQD measurement.
5.
Percussion Drilling: Heavy chisel bit dropped repeatedly into borehole to pulverize boulders, hardpan, and coarse gravel.
6.
Geophysical Methods: Non-destructive seismic refraction and electrical resistivity surveys for rapid preliminary reconnaissance across large infrastructure alignments.
Q.5 (c) 2025 7M Theory / Numerical 2x
Discuss Rock Mass Rating. How is it useful in finding the bearing capacity of rocks? The drilling carried out in a borehole from 6.00 m to 7.50 m below the ground level shows the 10 rock pieces of size 6, 8, 9, 10, 15, 18, 22 and 32 (all in centimeters). Determine the rock core recovery and rock quality designation. Comment on the quality of rock.
1.
Rock Mass Rating (RMR - Bieniawski): A geomechanical classification system that evaluates rock mass quality on a scale of 0 to 100 based on 6 core parameters: Uniaxial compressive strength of intact rock, Rock Quality Designation (RQD), Spacing of discontinuities, Condition of discontinuities (roughness, separation, infilling, weathering), Groundwater conditions, and Joint orientation adjustment. RMR provides empirical correlations for allowable rock bearing capacity, tunnel support, and deformation modulus.
2.
Core Run Calculation: Drill run length L = 7.50 m - 6.00 m = 1.50 m = 150 cm.
Sum of all 10 recovered rock core pieces (6, 8, 9, 10, 15, 18, 22, 32 cm + remaining pieces) = 120 cm.
Total Core Recovery (TCR):
$$TCR = \frac{\text{Total length of all recovered core pieces}}{\text{Total drill run length}} \times 100\% = \frac{120}{150} \times 100\% = \mathbf{80.0\%}$$
.
3.
Rock Quality Designation (RQD - Deere): Only sound core pieces of length ≥ 10 cm are summed:
Core pieces ≥ 10 cm: 10, 15, 18, 22, 32 cm.
$$\sum L_{pieces \ge 10 cm} = 10 + 15 + 18 + 22 + 32 = \mathbf{97 cm}$$
.
$$RQD = \frac{\sum L_{pieces \ge 10 cm}}{\text{Total drill run length}} \times 100\% = \frac{97}{150} \times 100\% = \mathbf{64.67\%}$$
.
4.
Comment on Rock Quality: According to Deere's RQD Engineering Classification:
•
< 25%: Very Poor
•
25% - 50%: Poor
50% - 75%: Fair:
•
75% - 90%: Good
•
90% - 100%: Excellent
Since RQD = 64.67%, the rock stratum between 6.00 m and 7.50 m is classified as FAIR QUALITY ROCK.
Q.5 (c) OR 2025 7M Theory / Numerical 4x
Explain the Standard Penetration Test. What are the different corrections to be applied to observed SPT value?
Following the observations of Standard Penetration Tests conducted at a site on sandy soil. Find the corrected N values.
Depth: 1.50 m, Observed SPT: 12, Density: 15.5 kN/m³
Depth: 3.00 m, Observed SPT: 18, Density: 17.2 kN/m³
Depth: 4.50 m, Observed SPT: 26, Density: 19.0 kN/m³
Depth: 6.00 m, Observed SPT: 32, Density: 20.5 kN/m³
1.
Standard Penetration Test (SPT - IS: 2131): A standard split-spoon sampler (OD 50.8 mm, ID 35 mm) is driven into the bottom of a borehole using a 63.5 kg hammer falling freely from 750 mm height. The sampler is driven 450 mm in three 150 mm increments. The first 150 mm is seating drive (ignored). The sum of blows for the last 300 mm is the observed N-value.
2. Standard Corrections:
•
Overburden Pressure Correction (Liao & Whitman / Peck):
$$N' = C_N \cdot N_0 = \sqrt{\frac{100}{\sigma'_v}} \cdot N_0 \quad \text{or} \quad N' = N_0 \cdot \frac{350}{\sigma'_v + 70} \quad (\text{for } \sigma'_v \le 280\text{ kPa})$$
.
•
Dilatancy / Water Table Correction: Applied if N' > 15 in saturated fine sand or silt below the water table:
$$N'' = 15 + 0.5 (N' - 15)$$
.
3.
Calculation Table for Given Site Data:
Depth (m) Density γ σ'v (kPa) Observed N CN = 350/(σ'v+70) N' = CN × N Corrected N (IS: 2131)
1.50 m 15.5 kN/m³ 15.5 × 1.5 = 23.25 12 350 / 93.25 = 3.75 (max 2.0) → 2.0 2.0 × 12 = 24 24
3.00 m 17.2 kN/m³ 23.25 + 17.2(1.5) = 49.05 18 350 / 119.05 = 2.94 (max 2.0) → 2.0 2.0 × 18 = 36 36
4.50 m 19.0 kN/m³ 49.05 + 19.0(1.5) = 77.55 26 350 / 147.55 = 2.37 (max 2.0) → 2.0 2.0 × 26 = 52 52
6.00 m 20.5 kN/m³ 77.55 + 20.5(1.5) = 108.30 32 350 / 178.30 = 1.96 1.96 × 32 = 63 63
•
If water table is present and dilatancy applies (fine sand/silt when N' > 15):
Depth 1.5m: N'' = 15 + 0.5(24 - 15) = 20.
Depth 3.0m: N'' = 15 + 0.5(36 - 15) = 26.
Depth 4.5m: N'' = 15 + 0.5(52 - 15) = 34.
Depth 6.0m: N'' = 15 + 0.5(63 - 15) = 39.

Unit 1 Lateral Earth Pressure 0/5
Q.1 (a) 2024 2M Theory 3x
List out the three types of earth pressure by giving examples.
Three Types of Earth Pressure with Examples:
1.
Active Earth Pressure: Pressure exerted by soil when the retaining wall moves away from the backfill.
Example: A retaining wall tilting away from soil.
2.
Passive Earth Pressure: Resistance offered by soil when the retaining wall moves towards the backfill.
Example: Soil resisting the movement of a sheet pile wall.
3.
Earth Pressure at Rest: Pressure exerted by soil when the retaining wall does not move.
Example: Basement walls restrained by rigid supports.
Q.1 (b) 2024 2M Theory 2x
List out the assumptions of Coulomb's theory.
Assumptions of Coulomb's Earth Pressure Theory:
1.
Soil is homogeneous and isotropic.
2.
Soil is dry and cohesionless.
3.
Backfill surface is a plane.
4.
Failure surface is a plane passing through the heel of the wall.
5.
Wall surface is straight and rigid.
6.
Friction develops between the wall and soil.
7.
Soil wedge behaves as a rigid body at failure.
Q.1 (c) 2024 3M Derivation
Derive an expression for earth pressure at-rest condition.
Derive Expression for Earth Pressure at Rest (3 Marks):
At-rest earth pressure occurs when the retaining wall does not move (zero lateral strain: εx = εy = 0).
1.
Vertical Stress at Depth z:
$$\sigma_v = \gamma z$$
2.
Horizontal Lateral Stress:
$$\sigma_h = K_0 \sigma_v = K_0 \gamma z$$
3.
Elastic Theory Derivation: From 3D Hooke's Law with zero lateral strain:
$$\varepsilon_x = \frac{1}{E}[\sigma_h - \mu(\sigma_h + \sigma_v)] = 0 \implies K_0 = \frac{\sigma_h}{\sigma_v} = \frac{\mu}{1 - \mu}$$
4.
Using Jaky's Equation (Normally Consolidated Soil):
$$K_0 = 1 - \sin\phi \implies \sigma_h = (1 - \sin\phi) \gamma z$$
5.
Total Earth Thrust (P0) at Wall Height H:
$$P_0 = \frac{1}{2} K_0 \gamma H^2 = \frac{1}{2} (1 - \sin\phi) \gamma H^2$$

Point of application acts at H/3 above the base.
Q.1 (d) 2024 7M Numerical 4x
A gravity retaining wall retains 12 m of a backfill. γ = 18 kN/m³, φ = 30° with a uniform horizontal backfill. Assuming the wall interface to be vertical, determine the magnitude of active and passive earth pressure. Assume the angle of wall friction to be 20°. Determine the point of action also.
Given Parameters:
Height H = 12 m, γ = 18 kN/m³, φ = 30°, δ = 20°, vertical wall face (α = 90°), horizontal backfill (β = 0°).
1.
Coulomb's Active Pressure Coefficient (Ka):
$$K_{a} = \cos ^2\phi / [ \cos \delta \cdot (1 + \sqrt{\sin (\phi + \delta }\sin \phi / \cos \delta ))^2 ]$$

$$\sin (\phi +\delta ) = \sin 50^\circ = 0.7660, \sin 30^\circ = 0.500, \cos 20^\circ = 0.9397$$

$$\sqrt{(0.7660 \times 0.500) / 0.9397} = \sqrt{0.4076} = 0.6384$$

$$K_{a} = \cos ^2 30^\circ / [0.9397 \times (1 + 0.6384)^2] = 0.750 / [0.9397 \times 2.6845] = 0.750 / 2.5228 \approx 0.2973$$
Total Active Thrust:
$$P_{a} = 0.5 \cdot K_{a} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 0.2973 \times 18 \times 12^2 = 385.3\text{ kN/m}$$

Acting at H/3 = 12/3 = 4.0 m above the base, inclined at δ = 20° downward to the normal.
2.
Coulomb's Passive Pressure Coefficient (Kp):
$$K_{p} = \cos ^2\phi / [ \cos \delta \cdot (1 - \sqrt{\sin (\phi + \delta }\sin \phi / \cos \delta ))^2 ] = 0.750 / [0.9397 \times (1 - 0.6384)^2] = 0.750 / [0.9397 \times 0.1308] \approx 6.103$$
Total Passive Thrust:
$$P_{p} = 0.5 \cdot K_{p} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 6.103 \times 18 \times 144 = 7909.5\text{ kN/m}$$

Acting at 4.0 m above the base, inclined at δ = 20° upward to the normal.
Q.1 (e) OR 2024 7M Numerical
A retaining wall is battered away from the fill from bottom to top at an angle of 15° with the vertical. Height of the wall is 6 m. The fill slopes upwards at an angle 15° away from the rest of the wall. The friction angle is 30° and wall friction angle is 15°. Using Coulomb's wedge theory, determine the total active and passive thrusts on the wall, per lineal metre assuming γ = 20 kN/m³.
Given Parameters:
Height H = 6 m, γ = 20 kN/m³, φ = 30°, δ = 15°, backfill slope β = 15°, wall batter α = 90° - 15° = 75°.
1.
Coulomb Active Thrust: Use Coulomb's general formula for inclined wall and sloping backfill:
$$K_{a} = \sin ^2(\alpha + \phi ) / [ \sin ^2\alpha \cdot \sin (\alpha - \delta ) \cdot [1 + \sqrt{\sin (\phi +\delta }\sin (\phi -\beta ) / (\sin (\alpha -\delta )\sin (\alpha +\beta )))]^2 ]$$

Substituting values yields
$$K_{a} \approx 0.448$$
.
$$P_{a} = 0.5 \cdot K_{a} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 0.448 \times 20 \times 6^2 = 161.3\text{ kN/m}$$
.
Line of action is at H/3 = 2.0 m above the base, inclined at δ = 15° to the wall normal.
2.
Coulomb Passive Thrust: Using Coulomb's passive coefficient with reversed friction signs:
$$K_{p} \approx 4.85$$
.
$$P_{p} = 0.5 \cdot K_{p} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 4.85 \times 20 \times 36 = 1746.0\text{ kN/m}$$
.
Unit 2 Shear Strength & Slope Stability 0/5
Q.2 (a) 2024 2M Theory
List the factors affecting the factor of safety of an infinite slope in a clay soil.
Factors Affecting Factor of Safety of Infinite Slope in Clay:
1.
Slope Angle (β): Steeper slope angle increases gravitational shear stress along the slip plane, reducing the factor of safety.
2.
Soil Cohesion (c'): Cohesion provides the primary shearing resistance in clay; higher cohesion directly increases the factor of safety.
3.
Depth of Slip Plane (H): In clay slopes, factor of safety decreases with depth because driving weight increases faster than cohesive resistance.
4.
Groundwater Seepage & Pore Pressure: Seepage creates pore water pressure, reducing effective normal stress and cutting safety by up to 50%.
5.
Unit Weight of Soil (γ): Higher unit weight of saturated soil increases the downslope driving force.
Q.2 (b) 2024 2M Theory 3x
What are different types of shear failure? Draw the sketches.
Three Types of Shear Failure in Soil:
1.
General Shear Failure: Occurs in dense sand and stiff clay. Continuous failure surface extends from footing edge to ground surface with distinct soil bulging and sudden tilting.
2.
Local Shear Failure: Occurs in medium dense sand and medium clay. Failure surfaces terminate within the soil mass, resulting in slight ground heave and gradual settlement.
3.
Punching Shear Failure: Occurs in loose sand and soft clay. Footing sinks vertically straight down into the soil by perimeter shearing, with zero ground heave and continuous plunging settlement.
Figure: Modes of Shear Failure & Rupture Surfaces
Q.2 (c) 2024 3M Theory 4x
Explain the classification of shear tests based on drainage condition.
Classification of Shear Tests by Drainage Condition:
IS: 2720
1.
Unconsolidated Undrained (UU / Quick Test): Drainage valve is kept closed during both cell pressure application and shearing. Water cannot escape. Test is fast (5-10 min) and measures undrained strength (cu).
Example: Foundation safety right after fast construction on saturated clay.
2.
Consolidated Undrained (CU Test): Drainage is allowed during cell pressure (complete consolidation), then the valve is closed during shearing while measuring pore pressure (u). Measures both total and effective parameters.
Example: Sudden reservoir water level drawdown behind an earth dam.
3.
Consolidated Drained (CD / Slow Test): Drainage is allowed throughout both stages. Shearing is very slow so no excess pore pressure builds up. Measures long-term drained parameters (c', φ').
Example: Long-term permanent stability of clay slopes after many years.
Q.2 (d) 2024 7M Theory
Illustrate different methods for improving the stability of slopes.
Methods for Improving Stability of Slopes:
1.
Slope Reshaping (Geometric Method): Flattening the slope angle, adding horizontal berms/benches, and removing weight from the top (crest) while loading the toe.
2.
Drainage Control (Most Effective): Providing surface ditches to catch rainwater, and deep horizontal perforated drains to lower the groundwater table and eliminate seepage forces.
3.
Retaining Structures: Building RCC retaining walls, gabions, or sheet piles at the toe to physically stop sliding.
4.
Soil Nailing & Reinforcement: Inserting steel rods (soil nails) with shotcrete facing, or placing geogrids in compacted fill slopes.
5.
Bio-Engineering: Planting deep-rooted grass (vetiver) to bind surface soil and prevent rain erosion.
Q.2 (e) OR 2024 7M Numerical
A cylindrical sample of soil of 50 mm in diameter and 100 mm long was subjected to axial and radial effective stresses. When the vertical displacement was 2 mm, the soil failed. The stresses at failure are σ₁ = 280 kPa and σ₃ = 100 kPa. The change in soil volume at failure was 800 mm³. Determine (a) Axial and volumetric strain at failure (b) Friction angle (c) The inclination of the slip plane to the horizontal.
Initial Sample Geometry:
d = 50 mm ⇒ A0 = (π/4) × 50² = 1963.5 mm², L0 = 100 mm ⇒ V0 = A0 × L0 = 196,350 mm³.
(a. Strains at Failure:
•
Axial Strain εa = ΔL / L0 = 2 mm / 100 mm = 0.02 (2.0%).
•
Volumetric Strain εv = ΔV / V0 = 800 mm³ / 196,350 mm³ = 0.00407 (0.407%).
(b.
Friction Angle (φ): For cohesionless soil (c = 0):
$$\sigma _1 / \sigma _3 = \tan ^2(45^\circ + \phi /2)$$

$$280 / 100 = 2.80 \implies \tan (45^\circ + \phi /2) = \sqrt{2.80} = 1.6733$$

$$45^\circ + \phi /2 = \arctan (1.6733) = 59.14^\circ \implies \phi = 2 \times (59.14^\circ - 45^\circ) = \mathbf{28.28^\circ}$$
.
(c.
Inclination of Slip Plane to Horizontal: Slip plane inclination θ = 45° + φ/2 = 59.14°.
Unit 3 Shallow Foundations 0/5
Q.3 (a) 2024 2M Theory 3x
List out the major criteria to be satisfied in the design of the foundation.
Major Design Criteria for Foundations:
1.
Shear Failure Criterion: Foundation must have an adequate factor of safety (FOS ≥ 2.5 to 3.0) against shear failure of supporting soil under maximum applied loads.
2.
Settlement Criterion: Total and differential settlements must stay within safe permissible limits specified by codes (IS: 1904) to prevent structural damage or distortion.
3.
Depth Criterion: Foundation must be placed at sufficient depth below topsoil, frost line, and seasonal moisture swelling/shrinkage zone (minimum depth ≥ 0.5 m to 1.0 m).
4.
Location & Environmental Safety: Foundation must be safe against scour from flowing water, erosion, and undermining from adjacent excavations.
Q.3 (b) 2024 2M Theory
Write brief notes on 'Settlement of foundation'.
Settlement of Foundation:
Total foundation settlement consists of three components:
$$S_{total} = S_i + S_c + S_s$$
1.
Immediate (Elastic) Settlement (Si): Occurs instantly upon load application due to elastic deformation without change in water content.
2.
Primary Consolidation Settlement (Sc): Time-dependent settlement in saturated clay caused by the gradual expulsion of pore water under sustained load.
3.
Secondary Settlement (Ss): Very slow plastic deformation of soil skeleton occurring after excess pore water pressure has fully dissipated.
4.
Permissible Limits: Maximum permissible total settlement for isolated footings is 40 mm in sand and 65 mm in clay (per IS: 1904).
Q.3 (c) 2024 3M Theory
Explain the failures in the shallow foundations.
Failures in Shallow Foundations:
1.
Soil Shear Failure: General shear (sudden tilting), local shear (gradual sinking), or punching shear (vertical plunge).
2.
Settlement Failure: Excessive total settlement damages connected pipes; unequal differential settlement causes wall cracks, building tilt, and jammed doors.
3.
Structural Footing Failure: Footing concrete slab cracks due to excessive upward bending or column punching through the slab.
Q.3 (d) 2024 7M Numerical
Two load tests were conducted at a site—one with a 0.5 m square test plate and the other with a 1.0 m square test plate. For a settlement of 25 mm, the loads were found to be 60 kN and 180 kN respectively in the two tests. Determine the allowable bearing pressure of the sand and the load which a square footing, 2 m × 2 m can carry with the settlement not exceeding 25 mm.
Housel's Equation:
$$Q = A \cdot m + P \cdot n$$

where A = plate area, P = plate perimeter, m = perimeter shear resistance factor, n = base resistance factor.
Test 1 (0.5 m square plate):
A1 = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 m², P1 = 4 × 0.5 = 2.0 m, Q1 = 60 kN.
$$60 = 0.25\text{ m} + 2.0 n   — (Equation 1)$$
Test 2 (1.0 m square plate):
A2 = 1.0 × 1.0 = 1.0 m², P2 = 4 × 1.0 = 4.0 m, Q2 = 180 kN.
$$180 = 1.0\text{ m} + 4.0 n   — (Equation 2)$$

Multiply Eq. 1 by 2:
$$120 = 0.5\text{ m} + 4.0 n$$
.
Subtract from Eq. 2:
$$60 = 0.5\text{ m} \implies m = 120\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Substitute into Eq. 1:
$$60 = 0.25(120) + 2n \implies 60 = 30 + 2n \implies n = 15\text{ kN/m}$$
.
For Footing (2.0 m × 2.0 m):
A = 2 × 2 = 4.0 m², P = 4 × 2 = 8.0 m.
$$Q_{footing} = 4.0(120) + 8.0(15) = 480 + 120 = \mathbf{600\text{ kN}}$$
.
Allowable Bearing Pressure:
$$q_{a} = Q / A = 600 / 4.0 = \mathbf{150\text{ kN/m}^2 (150\text{ kPa})}$$
.
Q.3 (e) OR 2024 7M Numerical 4x
A strip footing of 2.2 m width is to be founded at a depth of 1.2 m below GL. The soil profile shows the highest possible location of the water table at the site is estimated to be at 0.8 m below GL. The soil profile shows the presence of 0.5 m thick layer of fill material (γ = 14.8 kN/m³), which is underlain by a deep sand stratum having the following average properties: φ = 25°, e = 0.99, G = 2.72, water content above water table = 5%. Determine the safe bearing capacity of the footing with respect to a factor of safety of 2.5.
1.
Sand Unit Weights: Moist sand above WT (w = 5% = 0.05):
$$\gamma = G\frac{1+w}{1+e} \cdot \gamma _{w} = 2.72(1.05)/1.99 \times 9.81 = 14.07\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
Submerged sand below WT:
$$\gamma ' = \frac{G - 1}{1 + e} \cdot \gamma _{w} = \frac{2.72 - 1}{1.99} \times 9.81 = 8.48\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
2.
Effective Surcharge at Foundation Base (Df = 1.2 m): Fill (0 to 0.5 m):
$$0.5 \times 14.8 = 7.4\text{ kPa}$$
.
Moist sand (0.5 to 0.8 m):
$$0.3 \times 14.07 = 4.22\text{ kPa}$$
.
Submerged sand (0.8 to 1.2 m):
$$0.4 \times 8.48 = 3.39\text{ kPa}$$
.
Total effective surcharge
$$q = 7.4 + 4.22 + 3.39 = 15.01\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
3.
Bearing Capacity (Terzaghi Strip Footing): For φ = 25°: Nq = 10.66, Nγ = 10.88, c = 0.
$$q_{ult} = q \cdot N_{q} + 0.5 \cdot \gamma ' \cdot B \cdot N_{\gamma }$$

$$q_{ult} = (15.01 \times 10.66) + 0.5 \times (8.48) \times 2.2 \times 10.88 = 160.0 + 101.5 = 261.5\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{net_ult} = 261.5 - 15.01 = 246.5\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Safe Bearing Capacity (FS = 2.5):
$$q_{safe} = (q_{net_ult} / 2.5) + q = (246.5 / 2.5) + 15.01 = 98.6 + 15.01 = \mathbf{113.61\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Unit 4 Deep Foundations (Piles) 0/5
Q.4 (a) 2024 2M Theory
Write short notes on group action of piles.
Group Action of Piles:
1.
Group Action: Piles are installed in clusters connected by a rigid pile cap to transmit heavy structural loads into the ground.
2.
Stress Overlap: Stress zones of closely spaced individual piles overlap in the soil, which can reduce individual pile efficiency and increase group settlement.
3.
Failure Modes: A pile group in clay may fail either by individual pile failure (Qg = n · Qu) or as one large solid block (Qblock). Design capacity is the lesser of the two.
4.
Group Efficiency (ηg): Ratio of group capacity to the sum of individual capacities: ηg = Qgroup / (n · Qsingle) × 100%. In sand ηg > 100%, while in clay ηg ≤ 100%.
5.
Pile Spacing: Standard center-to-center spacing is 2.5 to 3.5 times the pile diameter for friction piles.
Q.4 (b) 2024 2M Theory
Describe about under-reamed pile foundation.
Under-Reamed Pile Foundation:
1.
Definition: Bored cast-in-situ concrete piles with one or more enlarged bulbs (under-reams) along their shaft.
2.
Primary Application: Specially designed for expansive soils (Black Cotton soil) that undergo severe swelling in monsoon and shrinkage in summer.
3.
Bulb Dimensions: Bulb diameter is typically 2.0 to 2.5 times the stem diameter, drilled using an under-reaming tool.
4.
Anchorage Mechanism: The bulb is anchored deep below the active seasonal moisture zone (> 1.5 m to 3.5 m) to resist upward swelling and pullout forces.
5.
Load Capacity: Enlarged bulb provides a large base bearing area for downward compressive loads and high uplift resistance.
Q.4 (c) 2024 3M Theory
Explain an 'Open Caisson' with a neat sketch showing all the component parts.
Open Caisson (Well Foundation) Components:
Open Caisson: A hollow box or cylinder structure, open at top and bottom, sunk into riverbeds by dredging soil from inside, then sealed with concrete at the bottom. Used for heavy bridge piers.
1.
Cutting Edge: Hardened steel angle at bottom to cut soil during sinking.
2.
Well Curb: Concrete wedge guiding soil into the well.
3.
Steining: Thick wall providing sinking weight.
4.
Dredge Hole: Central opening for excavating soil.
5.
Bottom Plug: Concrete seal placed underwater at founding depth to transfer pier load.
6.
Sand Filling: Clean sand placed inside well for ballast and stability.
7.
Top Plug: Concrete slab placed over sand filling.
8.
Well Cap: Top RCC slab supporting the bridge pier.
Figure: Cross-Section of Open Caisson (Well Foundation) Components
Q.4 (d) 2024 7M Numerical 2x
A square group of 9 piles was driven into soft clay extending to a large depth. The diameter and length of the piles were 30 cm and 9 m respectively. If the unconfined compression strength of the clay is 90 kN/m², and the pile spacing is 90 cm centre to centre, determine the capacity of the pile group? Assume a factor of safety of 2.5 and adhesion factor of 0.75.
Given Parameters:
Group configuration = 3 × 3 = 9 piles, d = 0.30 m, L = 9.0 m, spacing s = 0.90 m, qu = 90 kN/m² ⇒ c = qu/2 = 45 kN/m², α = 0.75, FS = 2.5.
1.
Individual Pile Failure Mode (Qgi): Base area Ab = (π/4)(0.3)² = 0.07068 m².
Surface area As = π × 0.3 × 9.0 = 8.482 m².
Single pile ultimate:
$$Q_{u} = 9 c A_{b} + \alpha c A_{s}$$

$$Q_{u} = 9(45)(0.07068) + 0.75(45)(8.482) = 28.63 + 286.28 = 314.91\text{ kN}$$
.
Total for 9 piles:
$$Q_{gi} = 9 \times 314.91 = \mathbf{2834.2\text{ kN}}$$
.
2.
Block Failure Mode (Qgb): Block width B = 2s + d = 2(0.9) + 0.3 = 2.1 m.
Block base area Ag = B² = 2.1² = 4.41 m².
Block perimeter Pg = 4B = 4(2.1) = 8.4 m.
$$Q_{gb} = 9 c B^2 + c P_{g} L = 9(45)(4.41) + 45(8.4)(9.0) = 1786.05 + 3402.0 = \mathbf{5188.05\text{ kN}}$$
.
3.
Governing Ultimate & Safe Capacity: Governing Qug = min(2834.2, 5188.05) = 2834.2 kN (Individual failure governs).
Safe capacity = 2834.2 / 2.5 = 1133.7 kN.
Q.4 (e) OR 2024 7M Numerical
A 16-pile group has to be arranged in the form of a square in soft clay with uniform spacing. Neglecting end-bearing, determine the optimum value of the spacing of the piles in terms of the pile diameter, assuming a shear mobilisation factor of 0.6.
Derivation of Optimum Spacing:
16 piles in square group (4 × 4 array). Let d = pile diameter, s = center-to-center spacing, L = pile length, c = clay cohesion, α = 0.6.
Neglecting end-bearing (friction piles only):
1.
Capacity by Individual Action:
$$Q_{gi} = 16 \cdot (\alpha \cdot c \cdot \pi \cdot d \cdot L) = 16 \times 0.6 \times \pi \cdot d \cdot L \cdot c = 9.6 \pi \cdot d \cdot L \cdot c \approx 30.16 \cdot d \cdot L \cdot c$$
.
2.
Capacity by Block Action: Width of block B = 3s + d. Block perimeter Pg = 4(3s + d).
$$Q_{gb} = P_{g} \cdot L \cdot c = 4(3s + d) \cdot L \cdot c$$
.
3.
Equating for Optimum Spacing: At optimum spacing, individual capacity equals block capacity:
$$4(3s + d) \cdot L \cdot c = 30.16 \cdot d \cdot L \cdot c$$

$$12 s + 4 d = 30.16 d \implies 12 s = 26.16 d \implies s = (26.16 / 12) d \approx \mathbf{2.18 d}$$
.
Therefore, optimum spacing is s ≈ 2.2 d.
Unit 5 Soil Exploration & Testing 0/5
Q.5 (a) 2024 2M Theory 2x
List out the objectives of soil exploration.
Objectives of Soil Exploration:
1.
To determine the depth, thickness, and extent of each soil and rock stratum across the site.
2.
To locate the groundwater table and monitor its seasonal fluctuations.
3.
To obtain disturbed and undisturbed soil samples for identification and laboratory testing.
4.
To evaluate engineering properties of soil (shear strength, compressibility, permeability, and bearing capacity).
5.
To select the most suitable, safe, and economical type and depth of foundation.
6.
To identify potential construction hazards (excavation collapse, dewatering requirements, expansive soils).
Q.5 (b) 2024 2M Theory
Sketch a typical borelog and describe its features.
Typical Borelog Layout and Features:
1.
Header Information: Project title, borehole number (BH-01), ground surface elevation (RL), date of boring, and drilling method.
2.
Strata Description: Layer depth boundaries, thickness, and standard engineering classification/symbols of each stratum.
3.
Groundwater Level: Exact depth where groundwater table (GWT) was encountered during drilling and stabilized.
4.
Sampling & Field Test Data: Depth of collected samples, sample type (disturbed/undisturbed), and recorded SPT N-values.
Figure: Typical Soil Investigation Borelog Layout (IS: 1892)
Q.5 (c) 2024 3M Theory 2x
Explain inside clearance, outside clearance and area ratio.
Soil Sampler Criteria (IS: 1892):
Let D1 = inside tip dia, D2 = outside tip dia, D3 = inside tube dia, D4 = outside tube dia.
1.
Area Ratio (Ar): Represents volume of soil displaced during driving. For undisturbed samples, Ar ≤ 10% to 20%.
$$A_r = \frac{D_2^2 - D_1^2}{D_1^2} \times 100\%$$
2.
Inside Clearance (Ci): Allows sample to expand slightly inside tube, reducing wall friction and sticking (1% to 3%).
$$C_i = \frac{D_3 - D_1}{D_1} \times 100\%$$
3.
Outside Clearance (Co): Reduces friction between soil and outside tube during driving and extraction (0% to 2%).
$$C_o = \frac{D_2 - D_4}{D_4} \times 100\%$$
Q.5 (d) 2024 7M Theory
Describe about the depth of exploration required for various types of structures/foundations.
Depth of Exploration Required for Structures (IS: 1892):
1.
Significant Depth: Exploration must extend down to where vertical stress increase drops to 10% (0.1 q) of applied contact pressure.
2. Depth Guidelines:
•
Isolated Footing: 1.5 B to 2.0 B below base.
•
Raft Foundation: 1.5 times the raft width (W).
•
Pile Foundation: 1.5 times pile group width (Bg) below pile tips, or 5 m into rock.
•
Retaining Wall: 1.5 times wall height (H).
•
Earth Dam: 1.0 to 1.5 times dam height.
3.
Borehole Spacing: Multi-story buildings (15-30 m), Industrial plants (20-60 m), Highways (100-300 m), Dams (25-50 m).
Q.5 (e) OR 2024 7M Theory 4x
Describe a standard penetration test. What are the corrections applied?
Standard Penetration Test (SPT) & Required Corrections:
IS: 2131
1.
Procedure: Split-spoon sampler (50.8 mm OD, 35 mm ID) driven into borehole bottom by 63.5 kg hammer falling freely from 750 mm height in 3 intervals of 150 mm. First 150 mm is seating drive (ignored). Sum of blows for last 300 mm = Observed N-value (N0).
Figure: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) Setup per IS: 2131
2.
Correction 1: Overburden Pressure (N'): Normalizes N for depth confining stress:
$$N' = N_0 \times \frac{350}{\sigma'_v + 70} \qquad (\sigma'_v \le 280\text{ kPa})$$
3.
Correction 2: Dilatancy / Submergence (N''): Applied for saturated fine sand/silt below water table when N' > 15:
$$N'' = 15 + 0.5 (N' - 15)$$
2023 Paper 0 / 28 Done (0%)
Unit 1 Lateral Earth Pressure 0/6
Q.1 (a) 2023 2M Theory 3x
What are different Types of Earth Pressure and what are different theories of Earth Pressures?
1. Three Types of Lateral Earth Pressure (Based on Wall Movement):
a.
Active Earth Pressure (Pa): Lateral pressure exerted by soil when the retaining wall moves away from the backfill.
Example: A cantilever retaining wall tilting away from soil.
b.
Passive Earth Pressure (Pp): Lateral resistance offered by soil when the retaining wall moves towards the backfill.
Example: Soil resisting the movement of an anchor deadman or sheet pile.
c.
Earth Pressure at Rest (P0): Lateral pressure exerted by soil when the retaining wall undergoes zero lateral movement (εx = 0).
Example: Rigid basement walls restrained by floor slabs.
2. Two Classical Earth Pressure Theories:
a.
Rankine's Theory (1857): Considers plastic equilibrium of a semi-infinite soil mass, assuming a vertical, smooth (frictionless) wall back.
b.
Coulomb's Wedge Theory (1776): Considers equilibrium of a planar sliding rigid soil wedge, accounting for wall friction (δ) and inclined wall back.
Q.1 (b) i 2023 3M Numerical 2x
A smooth vertical wall, 6 m high supports an inclined non-cohesive backfill (φ = 32°; γ = 21 kN/m³) at an angle 10° with horizontal. Compute the total active & passive pressure at the bottom of wall.
Given Parameters:
H = 6 m, γ = 21 kN/m³, φ = 32°, backfill inclination β = 10°, smooth vertical wall.
1.
Rankine Surcharged Coefficients:
$$\cos \beta = \cos 10^\circ = 0.9848, \cos \phi = \cos 32^\circ = 0.8480$$

$$\sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi } = \sqrt{0.9698 - 0.7192} = \sqrt{0.2507} = 0.5007$$

$$K_{a} = \cos \beta \frac{\cos \beta - \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi }}{\cos \beta + \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi }} = 0.9848 \frac{0.9848 - 0.5007}{0.9848 + 0.5007} = 0.9848(0.4841) / 1.4855 = \mathbf{0.3210}$$
.
$$K_{p} = \cos \beta \frac{\cos \beta + \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi }}{\cos \beta - \sqrt{\cos ^2\beta - \cos ^2\phi }} = 0.9848(1.4855) / 0.4841 = \mathbf{3.0219}$$
.
2.
Intensities at Bottom of Wall (z = 6 m): Active intensity
$$p_{a} = K_{a} \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 0.3210 \times 21 \times 6 = \mathbf{40.45\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Passive intensity
$$p_{p} = K_{p} \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 3.0219 \times 21 \times 6 = \mathbf{380.76\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Q.1 (b) ii 2023 3M Numerical 4x
A rough vertical wall of 7.5 m height supports a horizontal backfill. If the angle of internal friction and angle of wall friction are respectively 33° and 12°, compute the passive earth pressure at the bottom of wall. Assume density of 18.5 kN/m³.
Given: H = 7.5 m, φ = 33°, δ = 12°, γ = 18.5 kN/m³, vertical back (α = 90°), horizontal backfill (β = 0°).
Coulomb Passive Coefficient Kp:
$$K_{p} = \cos ^2\phi / [ \cos \delta \cdot (1 - \sqrt{\sin (\phi +\delta ) \cdot \sin \phi / \cos \delta })^2 ]$$

$$\cos 33^\circ = 0.8387 \implies \cos ^2 33^\circ = 0.7034, \cos 12^\circ = 0.9781$$

$$\sin (\phi +\delta ) = \sin 45^\circ = 0.7071, \sin 33^\circ = 0.5446$$

$$\sqrt{(0.7071 \times 0.5446)/0.9781} = \sqrt{0.3851/0.9781} = \sqrt{0.3937} = 0.6275$$

$$K_{p} = 0.7034 / [0.9781 \times (1 - 0.6275)^2] = 0.7034 / [0.9781 \times 0.1388] = 0.7034 / 0.1358 = \mathbf{5.180}$$
.
Passive Pressure Intensity at Bottom (z = 7.5 m):
$$p_{p} = K_{p} \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 5.180 \times 18.5 \times 7.5 = \mathbf{718.7\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
(Total passive force Pp = 0.5 × 718.7 × 7.5 = 2695.2 kN/m).
Q.1 (b) iii 2023 3M Numerical 2x
A retaining wall of 4.5 m height carries a horizontal backfill with c = 35 kN/m², φ = 10°; γ = 17.2 kN/m³. The water table is located at 1.50 m below the ground. Sketch the distribution of active earth pressure. Assume the value of angle of internal friction is 14°; and cohesion c = 50 kN/m² in the submerged condition.
Stratification:
•
Zone 1 (0 to 1.5 m, above WT): c = 35 kPa, φ = 10°, γ = 17.2 kN/m³.
$$K_{a1} = \tan ^2(45^\circ - 5^\circ) = \tan ^2(40^\circ) = 0.7041, \sqrt{K_{a1}} = 0.8391$$
.
At z = 0:
$$p_{a} = 0 - 2(35)(0.8391) = -58.74\text{ kPa} (tension)$$
.
Tension crack depth:
$$z_{c} = 2c/(\gamma \sqrt{K_{a1}}) = 2(35) / [17.2 \times 0.8391] = 4.85\text{ m} > 1.5\text{ m}$$
.
At z = 1.5 m (just above WT):
$$p_{a} = (17.2 \times 1.5 \times 0.7041) - 58.74 = 18.17 - 58.74 = -40.57\text{ kPa}$$
.
•
Zone 2 (1.5 to 4.5 m, submerged): c = 50 kPa, φ = 14°, γsat ≈ 20 kN/m³ ⇒ γ' = 20 - 9.81 = 10.19 kN/m³.
$$K_{a2} = \tan ^2(45^\circ - 7^\circ) = \tan ^2(38^\circ) = 0.6107, \sqrt{K_{a2}} = 0.7815$$
.
At z = 4.5 m (effective surcharge σ'v = 17.2 × 1.5 + 10.19 × 3.0 = 25.8 + 30.57 = 56.37 kPa):
Effective soil thrust:
$$\sigma '_{a} = K_{a2} \cdot \sigma '_{v} - 2 c \sqrt{K_{a2}} = 0.6107(56.37) - 2(50)(0.7815) = 34.43 - 78.15 = -43.72\text{ kPa}$$
.
Hydrostatic pore water pressure:
$$u = \gamma _{w} \times 3.0 = 9.81 \times 3.0 = +29.43\text{ kPa}$$
.
Q.1 (c) 2023 6M Derivation 2x
Derive the condition of maximum active earth pressure from sliding wedge.
Condition of Maximum Active Earth Pressure (Sliding Wedge Method):
1. Forces Acting on Trial Soil Wedge:
•
Weight of wedge (W) acting vertically downwards.
•
Soil reaction (R) on the slip plane, inclined at angle φ to the normal.
•
Active earth thrust (Pa) on wall, inclined at wall friction angle δ to the normal.
2.
Force Equilibrium (Sine Rule): From the force triangle of the sliding wedge:
$$P_a = W \cdot \frac{\sin(\theta - \phi)}{\sin(\theta - \phi + \alpha + \delta)}$$

Where θ is the inclination of the trial failure plane.
3.
Condition for Critical Failure Plane: The actual failure plane exerts the maximum possible thrust on the wall. Differentiating Pa with respect to θ and setting to zero:
$$\frac{dP_a}{d\theta} = 0$$
4.
Result: For a vertical smooth wall (α = 90°, δ = 0) and level backfill, solving dPa/dθ = 0 gives:
$$\theta_{cr} = 45^\circ + \frac{\phi}{2} \qquad P_a = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 \left(\frac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi}\right)$$
Q.1 (c) OR 2023 6M Theory 3x
Explain the Rebhann's graphical construction for active earth pressure and prove that it satisfy the condition of maximum earth pressure.
Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Earth Thrust:
1.
Principle: A graphical method based on Poncelet's solution to find the critical failure plane and total Coulomb active thrust (Pa) directly without trial-and-error.
2. Step-by-Step Construction Procedure:
•
Step 1: Draw wall face AB and ground line AD.
•
Step 2: From heel B, draw φ-line BD at angle φ to horizontal, cutting ground at D.
•
Step 3: Draw ψ-line BL at angle ψ = β - δ to the φ-line.
•
Step 4: Draw a semi-circle with line BD as diameter.
•
Step 5: From crest A, draw line AE parallel to ψ-line, intersecting BD at E.
•
Step 6: At E, erect perpendicular EF cutting the semi-circle at F.
•
Step 7: With center B and radius BF, swing an arc to cut line BD at point C.
•
Step 8: Draw line CD parallel to ψ-line to cut ground line at D. Line BC is the critical failure plane!
3.
Graphical Construction Diagram:
Figure: Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Thrust (Pa)
4.
Total Active Earth Thrust:
$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area}(\triangle BCD) = \frac{1}{2} \gamma \cdot (CD) \cdot h'$$

Acting at H/3 above the base inclined at angle δ to the wall normal.
