Q.2 (b) i 2023 3M Theory 3x
Describe the three modes of shear failure in soil. Draw load-settlement curves for each mode and explain which type of soil exhibits each failure pattern.
Three Modes of Shear Failure & Load-Settlement Behavior:
1.
General Shear Failure: Dense sand (Dr > 70%) and stiff clay. Rupture surface extends to ground with surface heave. Curve has a sharp peak failure load (qu) followed by sudden drop.
2.
Local Shear Failure: Medium sand (35% < Dr < 70%). Rupture surface stops within soil mass; slight heave. Curve has no sharp peak, showing gradual yield.
3.
Punching Shear Failure: Loose sand (Dr < 35%) and soft clay. Footing punches straight down; zero heave. Curve plunges downward continuously.
Figure: Load-Settlement (q vs s) Curves for Modes of Failure

Figure: Modes of Shear Failure & Rupture Surfaces
Q.3 (a) 2023 2M Theory 2x
Discuss Coulomb's law of shear strength of soil.
Coulomb's Law of Shear Strength of Soil:
1.
Total Stress Equation (Coulomb, 1776): Shear strength (τ) consists of cohesive resistance and frictional resistance:
$$\tau = c + \sigma \tan\phi$$

where c = cohesion, σ = total normal stress on failure plane, φ = angle of internal friction.
2.
Effective Stress Equation (Terzaghi, 1925): Shear strength is governed by effective stress between soil grains:
$$\tau = c' + \sigma' \tan\phi' = c' + (\sigma - u) \tan\phi'$$

where c' = effective cohesion, σ' = effective normal stress, u = pore water pressure, φ' = effective friction angle.
3. Special Cases:
•
Pure Sand (c = 0): τ = σ tanφ
•
Saturated Clay in Undrained Shear (φ = 0): τ = cu
Q.3 (b) i 2023 3M Numerical 2x
The shear stress and normal stress at a failure plane in a cohesionless soil mass were found to be 4 kPa and 10 kPa respectively. Determine the resultant stress on failure plane and inclination of failure plane. Also compute the shear parameters.
Given Parameters:
Cohesionless soil ⇒ c = 0. Normal stress σ = 10 kPa, Shear stress τ = 4 kPa.
1.
Resultant Stress on Failure Plane:
$$R = \sqrt{\sigma ^2 + \tau ^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{100 + 16} = \sqrt{116} = \mathbf{10.77\text{ kPa}}$$
.
2.
Shear Parameters: Since c = 0:
$$\tau = \sigma \tan \phi \implies \tan \phi = \tau / \sigma = 4 / 10 = 0.40$$
.
$$\phi = \arctan (0.40) = \mathbf{21.80^\circ}$$
, and
$$c = 0$$
.
3.
Inclination of Failure Plane with Major Principal Plane (θ):
$$\theta = 45^\circ + \phi /2 = 45^\circ + (21.80^\circ/2) = 45^\circ + 10.90^\circ = \mathbf{55.90^\circ}$$
.
Q.3 (b) ii 2023 3M Numerical 2x
The deviator force to shear the soil specimen of 38 mm diameter and 76 mm height under a confining pressure of 100 kN/m² is 251 N while it shears under a deviator force of 327 N at a confining pressure of 200 kN/m². The deformation at the time of failure is respectively 2.0 mm and 5.2 mm. Determine the shear parameters. Determine the deviator stress under a confining pressure of 250 kPa.
Initial Dimensions:
d = 38 mm ⇒ A0 = (π/4)(0.038)² = 1.134 × 10⁻³ m², L0 = 76 mm.
Test 1 (σ₃ = 100 kPa):
ΔL₁ = 2.0 mm ⇒ ε₁ = 2.0/76 = 0.02632.
Corrected Area A₁ = A0/(1 - ε₁) = 1.134 × 10⁻³ / (1 - 0.02632) = 1.1647 × 10⁻³ m².
Deviator stress:
$$\sigma _{d1} = 251 \times 10⁻^3\text{ kN} / (1.1647 \times 10⁻^3\text{ m}^2) = 215.5\text{ kPa}$$
.
Major principal stress:
$$\sigma _1 = 100 + 215.5 = 315.5\text{ kPa}$$
.
Test 2 (σ₃ = 200 kPa):
ΔL₂ = 5.2 mm ⇒ ε₂ = 5.2/76 = 0.06842.
Corrected Area A₂ = 1.134 × 10⁻³ / (1 - 0.06842) = 1.2173 × 10⁻³ m².
Deviator stress:
$$\sigma _{d2} = 327 \times 10⁻^3 / (1.2173 \times 10⁻^3) = 268.6\text{ kPa}$$
.
Major principal stress:
$$\sigma _1 = 200 + 268.6 = 468.6\text{ kPa}$$
.
Solve for Shear Parameters:
$$\sigma _1 = \sigma _3 \tan ^2(45^\circ + \phi /2) + 2c \tan (45^\circ + \phi /2)$$
.
Subtracting equations:
$$(468.6 - 315.5) = (200 - 100) N_{\phi } \implies 153.1 = 100 N_{\phi } \implies N_{\phi } = 1.531$$
.
$$\tan (45^\circ + \phi /2) = \sqrt{1.531} = 1.2373 \implies 45^\circ + \phi /2 = 51.05^\circ \implies \mathbf{\phi = 12.1^\circ}$$
.
From Test 1:
$$315.5 = 100(1.531) + 2c(1.2373) \implies 162.4 = 2.4746 c \implies \mathbf{c = 65.63\text{ kPa}}$$
.
At σ₃ = 250 kPa:
$$\sigma _1 = 250(1.531) + 2(65.63)(1.2373) = 382.75 + 162.4 = 545.15\text{ kPa}$$
.
Deviator stress:
$$\sigma _{d} = \sigma _1 - \sigma _3 = 545.15 - 250 = \mathbf{295.15\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Q.3 (b) iii 2023 3M Theory 4x
Explain various kinds of triaxial tests. Which test is best suited for the cohesive soil deposit having a permeable layer immediately below the foundation level?
Kinds of Triaxial Tests & Suitability for Saturated Clay:
IS: 2720
1.
UU Test: No drainage allowed. Fast test (5-10 min). Gives undrained strength cu.
2.
CU Test: Consolidation allowed, then sheared undrained while measuring pore pressure u.
3.
CD Test: Drainage allowed in both stages. Very slow test (days to weeks).
4. Best Test for Saturated Clay:
Consolidated Undrained (CU) Test with pore pressure measurement.:
•
Reason: Saturated clay has low permeability, so a drained CD test takes weeks. The CU test allows consolidation, then shears quickly while measuring pore pressure u, giving both total and effective parameters (c', φ') in just one day.
Q.3 (c) 2023 6M Derivation 2x
Derive a relationship between effective shear parameters and principal stresses.
Relationship Between Effective Shear Parameters & Principal Stresses:
1. Mohr Circle Geometry at Failure:
•
Center: C = ((σ'1 + σ'3) / 2, 0)
•
Radius: R = (σ'1 - σ'3) / 2
2.
Right Triangle Relationship: In the right triangle formed by radius R and failure envelope inclined at φ' with intercept c':
$$\sin\phi' = \frac{\text{Radius}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{\frac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}}{\frac{c'}{\tan\phi'} + \frac{\sigma'_1 + \sigma'_3}{2}}$$
3.
Simplifying: Multiplying terms and grouping σ'1 and σ'3:
$$\sigma'_1(1 - \sin\phi') = \sigma'_3(1 + \sin\phi') + 2c'\cos\phi'$$
4.
Final Equation: Dividing by (1 - sinφ'):
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) + 2c'\tan\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right)$$
Q.3 (c) OR 2023 6M Numerical 2x
The following data refers to triaxial compression tests performed on a soil sample. Determine the total and effective shear parameters of soil. Observation 1: Cell Pressure = 80 kPa, Max Deviator Stress = 175 kPa, Pore Pressure at failure = 45 kPa. Observation 2: Cell Pressure = 150 kPa, Max Deviator Stress = 240 kPa, Pore Pressure at failure = 50 kPa. Observation 3: Cell Pressure = 300 kPa, Max Deviator Stress = 300 kPa, Pore Pressure at failure = 60 kPa.
1. Compilation of Stress States:
•
Test 1: σ₃ = 80 kPa, σ₁ = 80 + 175 = 255 kPa, u = 45 kPa ⇒ σ'₃ = 80 - 45 = 35 kPa, σ'₁ = 255 - 45 = 210 kPa.
•
Test 2: σ₃ = 150 kPa, σ₁ = 150 + 240 = 390 kPa, u = 50 kPa ⇒ σ'₃ = 150 - 50 = 100 kPa, σ'₁ = 390 - 50 = 340 kPa.
•
Test 3: σ₃ = 300 kPa, σ₁ = 300 + 300 = 600 kPa, u = 60 kPa ⇒ σ'₃ = 300 - 60 = 240 kPa, σ'₁ = 600 - 60 = 540 kPa.
2.
Effective Shear Parameters (c', φ'): Using Tests 1 and 2:
$$\Delta \sigma '_1 / \Delta \sigma '_3 = \frac{340 - 210}{100 - 35} = 130 / 65 = 2.0 = N_{\phi '}$$
.
$$\tan (45^\circ + \phi '/2) = \sqrt{2.0} = 1.414 \implies 45^\circ + \phi '/2 = 54.74^\circ \implies \mathbf{\phi ' = 19.5^\circ}$$
.
Substitute into Test 1:
$$210 = 35(2.0) + 2 c'(1.414) \implies 140 = 2.828 c' \implies \mathbf{c' = 49.5\text{ kPa}}$$
.
3.
Total Shear Parameters (c, φ): Using Tests 1 and 2:
$$\Delta \sigma _1 / \Delta \sigma _3 = \frac{390 - 255}{150 - 80} = 135 / 70 = 1.928 = N_{\phi }$$
.
$$\tan (45^\circ + \phi /2) = \sqrt{1.928} = 1.3887 \implies 45^\circ + \phi /2 = 54.24^\circ \implies \mathbf{\phi = 18.5^\circ}$$
.
Substitute into Test 1:
$$255 = 80(1.928) + 2 c(1.3887) \implies 100.7 = 2.777 c \implies \mathbf{c = 36.26\text{ kPa}}$$
.

Q.2 (a) 2023 2M Theory 2x
What do you mean by bearing capacity? What are the different suffixes to be used before bearing capacity?
Bearing Capacity Definitions and Common Suffixes:
Bearing Capacity: The load carrying capacity of soil per unit area without undergoing shear failure or excessive settlement.
1.
Ultimate Bearing Capacity (qu): The minimum gross contact pressure at which the supporting soil fails completely in shear.
2.
Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (qnet_u): The minimum net pressure above overburden pressure causing shear failure: qnet_u = qu - γDf.
3.
Safe Bearing Capacity (qsafe): The safe gross pressure on soil with an adequate factor of safety: qsafe = qnet_u / FOS + γDf.
4.
Allowable Bearing Capacity (qa): The maximum net pressure permitted on soil considering both shear failure safety and permissible settlement limits.
Q.2 (b) ii 2023 3M Theory 3x
Explain the effect of water table on bearing capacity of soils.
Effect of Water Table on Bearing Capacity (IS: 6403):
General equation with correction factors:
$$q_u = c N_c + \gamma_1 D_f N_q W^*_1 + 0.5 \gamma_2 B N_\gamma W^*_2$$
1.
Case 1 (Water Table at Ground Level): Entire soil is submerged (γ' ≈ 0.5 γsat). Bearing capacity drops by approximately 50%.
2.
Case 2 (Water Table Between Ground & Footing Base): Surcharge term uses weighted unit weight: W*1 = 0.5 [1 + dw / Df].
3.
Case 3 (Water Table Below Base within Depth B): Shear zone is partially submerged: W*2 = 0.5 [1 + zw / B].
4.
Case 4 (Water Table at Depth ≥ Df + B): Water table is below the failure zone; zero reduction in bearing capacity.
Q.2 (b) iii 2023 3M Numerical 2x
Compute the net safe bearing capacity of a square footing of size 2.5 m provided at 2.0 m depth in a purely cohesive soil with Unconfined Shear Strength of 150 kN/m² and density being 18 kN/m³. Use factor of safety as 2.5.
Given Parameters:
Square footing B = 2.5 m, Df = 2.0 m, γ = 18 kN/m³, FS = 2.5.
Purely cohesive soil: φ = 0°, cohesion
$$c = q_{u} / 2 = 150 / 2 = 75\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Terzaghi Bearing Capacity Factors for φ = 0°:
Nc = 5.7, Nq = 1.0, Nγ = 0.
For a square footing, ultimate bearing capacity:
$$q_{ult} = 1.3 c N_{c} + \gamma D_{f} N_{q} = 1.3(75)(5.7) + (18)(2.0)(1.0) = 555.75 + 36 = 591.75\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
$$q_{nu} = q_{ult} - \gamma D_{f} = 555.75\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Net Safe Bearing Capacity:
$$q_{ns} = q_{nu} / FS = 555.75 / 2.5 = \mathbf{222.3\text{ kN/m}^2 (kPa)}$$
.
(Using Skempton's Nc = 6.0(1 + 0.2 Df/B) = 6.0(1 + 0.16) = 6.96 ⇒ qns = 6.96 × 75 / 2.5 = 208.8 kN/m²).
Q.2 (c) 2023 6M Numerical 4x
A square footing of 3.5 m is resting at 3 m below the ground level. The shear parameters of soil are respectively 40 kN/m² and 12°. The density of soil is 20 kN/m³. The water table lies at 2 m below the base of footing. Calculate the net safe bearing capacity. Assume factor of safety of 3.0.
Given Parameters:
B = 3.5 m, Df = 3.0 m, c = 40 kN/m², φ = 12°, γ = 20 kN/m³, FS = 3.0.
Water table is at dw = 2.0 m below the footing base.
1.
Bearing Capacity Factors (Interpolated for φ = 12° from Table 1): From Table: φ=10° ⇒ (Nc=6.49, Nq=1.57, Nγ=0.45); φ=15° ⇒ (Nc=8.35, Nq=2.47, Nγ=1.22).
For φ = 12°:
$$N_{c} = 6.49 + (2/5)(8.35 - 6.49) = 7.23$$
.
$$N_{q} = 1.57 + (2/5)(2.47 - 1.57) = 1.93$$
.
$$N_{\gamma } = 0.45 + (2/5)(1.22 - 0.45) = 0.76$$
.
2.
Water Table Correction Factors: WT is below footing base ⇒ Rw1 = 1.0.
Since dw = 2.0 m < B = 3.5 m:
$$R_{w2} = 0.5 [1 + (d_{w} / B)] = 0.5 [1 + (2.0 / 3.5)] = 0.5 \times 1.5714 = 0.786$$
.
3.
Terzaghi Equation for Square Footing:
$$q_{ult} = 1.3 c N_{c} + \gamma D_{f} N_{q} \cdot R_{w1} + 0.4 \gamma B N_{\gamma } \cdot R_{w2}$$

$$q_{ult} = 1.3(40)(7.23) + (20)(3.0)(1.93)(1.0) + 0.4(20)(3.5)(0.76)(0.786)$$

$$q_{ult} = 375.96 + 115.80 + 16.73 = 508.49\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.

.
$$q_{ns} = q_{nu} / FS = 448.49 / 3.0 = \mathbf{149.50\text{ kN/m}^2 (kPa)}$$
.
Q.2 (c) OR 2023 6M Numerical 2x
A rectangular footing 3 m × 2 m carries a load of 1500 kN with eccentricity of 0.3 m along the length and 0.2 m along the width. The footing is located at 1.5 m depth in soil with c = 20 kN/m², φ = 25°, γ = 19 kN/m³. Calculate the maximum pressure at the base and check for safety.
Given Parameters:
L = 3.0 m, B = 2.0 m, Q = 1500 kN, eL = 0.3 m, eB = 0.2 m, Df = 1.5 m, c = 20 kPa, φ = 25°, γ = 19 kN/m³.
1.
Maximum Base Contact Pressure (Elastic Stress Formula):
$$q_{max} = (Q / A) \cdot [ 1 + (6 e_{L} / L) + (6 e_{B} / B) ]$$

Area A = 3 × 2 = 6 m².
$$6 e_{L} / L = 6(0.3)/3.0 = 0.60$$
,
$$6 e_{B} / B = 6(0.2)/2.0 = 0.60$$
.
$$q_{max} = (1500 / 6) \cdot [ 1 + 0.60 + 0.60 ] = 250 \times 2.20 = \mathbf{550.0\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
$$q_{min} = 250 \times [ 1 - 0.60 - 0.60 ] = -50\text{ kN/m}^2 (Tension at corner)$$
.
2.
Ultimate Capacity using Meyerhof's Effective Area Method: Effective dimensions:
$$L' = L - 2 e_{L} = 3.0 - 0.6 = 2.4\text{ m}$$
,
$$B' = B - 2 e_{B} = 2.0 - 0.4 = 1.6\text{ m}$$
.
Effective area A' = 2.4 × 1.6 = 3.84 m².
For φ = 25°: Nc = 20.2, Nq = 10.66, Nγ = 10.88.
Compute shape and depth factors; safe load Qsafe = qsafe × A'. If qmax ≤ qsafe, the footing is verified safe.
Q.4 (a) 2023 2M Theory 2x
What are different types of shallow foundations? Draw neat sketch of strap footing.
Types of Shallow Foundations and Strap Footing:
1. Types of Shallow Foundations:
•
Isolated column footing (pad, stepped, sloped)
•
Strip or continuous wall footing
•
Combined footing (rectangular or trapezoidal)
•
Strap (cantilever) footing
•
Raft (mat) foundation
2. Strap Footing Concept:
•
Used when an exterior column sits on a property line and its footing cannot extend outward.
•
A rigid RCC strap beam connects the eccentric exterior footing to an adjacent interior footing to prevent overturning.
•
The strap beam is suspended above ground (no contact with soil underneath) so it transfers bending moment and shear only.
Figure: Elevation & Structural Action of Strap (Cantilever) Footing
Q.4 (b) i 2023 3M Theory 3x
Enumerate the requirements of satisfactory foundations.
Requirements of Satisfactory Foundations (IS: 1904):
1.
Adequate Depth: Founded below topsoil, scour level, and seasonal moisture swelling/shrinkage zone.
2.
Safety Against Shear: Applied bearing pressure must not exceed safe bearing capacity (FOS ≥ 2.5 to 3.0).
3.
Safe Settlement: Total settlement ≤ 40 mm in sand, 65 mm in clay; differential angular distortion ≤ 1/500 to prevent wall cracks.
4.
Durability: Concrete and steel must resist groundwater chemical attack (sulfates per IS: 456).
Q.4 (b) ii 2023 3M Practical 2x
Two buildings are to be constructed at two different sites. First site shows the low compressive cohesive soil profile up to 10 m depth followed by good quality rock up to 15 m depth below the ground while the second site is having expansive soil up to 5 m depth followed by good rock up to 10 m below the ground. G+4 story building is to be constructed at the first site while at the second site G+15 story building is to be constructed. Suggest the type of foundation at two different sites for the structures to be constructed.
Foundation Recommendations for Two Site Conditions:
1. Site 1: Loose Sand with High Ground Water Table:
•
Recommendation: Raft (Mat) Foundation or Piles.
•
Reason: Loose sand has low strength and high settlement; water table cuts bearing capacity by 50% and causes liquefaction risk. A rigid raft bridges weak spots, or piles transfer loads to deep dense strata.
2. Site 2: Stiff Clay:
•
Recommendation: Isolated Spread Footings.
•
Reason: Stiff clay has high shear strength and low settlement. Isolated footings founded at 1.5 m to 2 m depth are safe, simple, and most economical.
Q.4 (b) iii 2023 3M Numerical 2x
Using the soil properties (γ = 17.5 kN/m³, c = 20 kN/m², φ = 20°), and assuming the square footing (3.415 m × 3.415 m) located at a depth of 1.5 m carries a total load of 2000 kN. Calculate the immediate settlement of the footing using the elastic theory. Assume the soil is homogeneous and isotropic with a Poisson's ratio of 0.3 and Young's modulus of 50,000 kN/m². (assume influence factor 0.88 for square footing)
Given Parameters:
Square footing B = 3.415 m, Area A = 3.415² = 11.662 m², Load Q = 2000 kN, Df = 1.5 m.
Soil properties: μ = 0.3, Es = 50,000 kN/m², Influence factor If = 0.88.
1.
Net Contact Pressure (q):
$$q = Q / A = 2000 / 11.662 = 171.50\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
2.
Elastic Settlement Equation (IS: 8009 Part 1):
$$S_{i} = [ q \cdot B \cdot (1 - \mu ^2) / E_{s} ] \cdot I_{f}$$

$$(1 - \mu ^2) = 1 - 0.3^2 = 1 - 0.09 = 0.91$$
.
$$S_{i} = [ (171.50 \times 3.415 \times 0.91) / 50000 ] \times 0.88$$

$$S_{i} = [ 532.96 / 50000 ] \times 0.88 = 0.010659 \times 0.88 = 0.00938\text{ m} = \mathbf{9.38\text{ mm}}$$
.
The immediate elastic settlement is 9.38 mm (well within the permissible limit of 25 mm).
Q.4 (c) OR 2023 6M Numerical 2x
Design a strip footing resting at 2.0 m below the ground and to carrying a load of 1000 kN/m, the shear parameters c = 50 kN/m² and angle of internal friction is 22° while the density is of soil is 20 kN/m³. The factor of safety to be used is 2.5.
Given Parameters:
Load per meter run Q' = 1000 kN/m, Df = 2.0 m, c = 50 kPa, φ = 22°, γ = 20 kN/m³, FS = 2.5.
1.
Bearing Capacity Factors (Interpolated for φ = 22° from Table 1): For φ = 22°: Nc ≈ 14.67, Nq ≈ 6.63, Nγ ≈ 5.94.
2.
Terzaghi Strip Footing Equation:
$$q_{ult} = c N_{c} + \gamma D_{f} N_{q} + 0.5 \gamma B N_{\gamma }$$

$$q_{ult} = 50(14.67) + 20(2.0)(6.63) + 0.5(20)(B)(5.94) = 733.5 + 265.2 + 59.4 B = 998.7 + 59.4 B$$
.
$$q_{nu} = q_{ult} - \gamma D_{f} = (998.7 + 59.4 B) - 40 = 958.7 + 59.4 B$$
.
$$q_{safe} = (q_{nu} / 2.5) + \gamma D_{f} = 383.48 + 23.76 B + 40 = 423.48 + 23.76 B$$
.
3.
Equate to Applied Pressure:
$$1000 / B = 423.48 + 23.76 B \implies 23.76 B^2 + 423.48 B - 1000 = 0$$
.
Solving the quadratic equation:
$$B = \frac{-423.48 + \sqrt{423.48^2 - 4(23.76}(-1000))}{2(23.76)}$$

$$\sqrt{ 179,335 + 95,040 } = \sqrt{274},375 = 523.81$$
.
$$B = (523.81 - 423.48) / 47.52 = 100.33 / 47.52 = \mathbf{2.11\text{ m}}$$
.

Design a square pile group to carry 500 kN load in clay with an unconfined compressive strength of 50 kN/m². Assume pile diameter of 400 mm and 6.0 m length. Adhesion factor may be taken as 0.6.
Given Parameters:
Design load Q = 500 kN, qu = 50 kPa ⇒ c = qu/2 = 25 kPa, d = 0.4 m, L = 6.0 m, α = 0.6. Adopt FS = 2.5.
1.
Single Pile Ultimate Capacity (Qu1): Base area Ab = (π/4)(0.4)² = 0.1257 m².
Surface area As = π × 0.4 × 6.0 = 7.540 m².
$$Q_{u1} = 9 c A_{b} + \alpha c A_{s} = 9(25)(0.1257) + 0.6(25)(7.540) = 28.28 + 113.10 = 141.38\text{ kN}$$
.
Allowable load per single pile:
$$Q_{all} = 141.38 / 2.5 = 56.55\text{ kN}$$
.
Number of piles required:
$$n = 500 / 56.55 = 8.84 \implies Select 9 piles (3 \times 3 square array)$$
.
2.
Group Geometry & Spacing: Adopt center-to-center spacing s = 3d = 3(0.4) = 1.2 m.
Block width B = 2s + d = 2(1.2) + 0.4 = 2.8 m.
3.
Check Block Failure Capacity: Block base area Ag = 2.8² = 7.84 m², Perimeter Pg = 4 × 2.8 = 11.2 m.
$$Q_{ug} = 9 c A_{g} + c P_{g} L = 9(25)(7.84) + 25(11.2)(6.0) = 1764.0 + 1680.0 = 3444.0\text{ kN}$$
.
Safe block capacity = 3444.0 / 2.5 = 1377.6 kN >> 500 kN (Extremely safe).

Unit 5 Soil Exploration & Testing 0/4
Q.5 (a) 2023 3M Theory 2x
Discuss different types of soil samples. How will you obtain undisturbed samples?
Types of Soil Samples & Obtaining Undisturbed Samples:
IS: 1892
1.
Disturbed Samples: Soil structure is broken, but soil mineral grains are intact. Used for sieve analysis, liquid limit, plastic limit.
2.
Undisturbed Samples: Natural soil structure, water content, and void ratio are preserved. Required for shear strength (c, φ), consolidation (Cc), and permeability.
3. How to Obtain Undisturbed Samples:
•
Use thin-walled tube sampler (Shelby tube) with area ratio Ar ≤ 10%.
•
Push smoothly into borehole base using hydraulic jack (never hammered).
•
Rotate to shear the base, extract, and seal ends immediately with molten paraffin wax (min 25 mm thick) and airtight caps.
Q.5 (b) 2023 4M Theory 3x
What do you understand by geotechnical exploration? What are the different methods of subsoil explorations?
Geotechnical Exploration — Meaning & Methods:
IS: 1892
Meaning: Investigating subsurface soil and rock layers to design safe, economical foundations.
1.
Direct Methods (Test Pits): Shallow open excavations (depth 3-6 m) for direct visual inspection.
2. Semi-Direct Methods (Borings):
•
Auger Boring: Hand or power auger rotated into clays above water table.
•
Wash Boring: Water jet chops soil inside casing; good for sand and soft clay.
•
Rotary Drilling: Rotating diamond bit with drilling mud; penetrates hard rock and extracts cores.
•
Percussion Drilling: Heavy chisel dropped repeatedly to break hard bouldery strata.
3.
Indirect Methods (Geophysical): Seismic refraction (wave velocity) and electrical resistivity for rapid preliminary surveying of large sites.
Q.5 (c) 2023 7M Numerical 2x
Discuss Rock Mass Rating. How is it useful in finding the bearing capacity of rocks? The drilling carried out in a borehole from 6.00 m to 7.50 m below the ground level shows the 10 rock pieces of size 6, 8, 9, 10, 15, 18, 22 and 32 (all in centimeters). Determine the rock core recovery and rock quality designation. Comment on the quality of rock.
1.
Rock Mass Rating (RMR - Bieniawski): A geomechanical classification based on 6 parameters: Uniaxial compressive strength of intact rock, RQD, Discontinuity spacing, Condition of discontinuities, Groundwater conditions, and Joint orientation adjustment. RMR provides safe rock bearing capacity and rock deformation modulus.
2.
Core Run Calculation: Drill run length L = 7.50 m - 6.00 m = 1.50 m = 150 cm.
Recovered pieces (cm): 6, 8, 9, 10, 15, 18, 22, 32 (and remaining 2 pieces: e.g. sum of 10 pieces = 120 cm).
Sum of all recovered rock core pieces = 6 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 15 + 18 + 22 + 32 = 120 cm.
Total Core Recovery (TCR):
$$TCR = (Total length of all core pieces / Drill run length) \times 100% = (120 / 150) \times 100% = \mathbf{80.0%}$$
.
3.
Rock Quality Designation (RQD - Deere): Only sound core pieces of length ≥ 10 cm are counted: 10, 15, 18, 22, 32 cm.
Sum of pieces ≥ 10 cm = 10 + 15 + 18 + 22 + 32 = 97 cm.
$$RQD = (Sum of lengths of core pieces \ge 10 cm / Drill run length) \times 100% = (97 / 150) \times 100% = \mathbf{64.67%}$$
.
4.
Comment on Rock Quality: According to Deere's classification (RQD 0-25%: Very Poor, 25-50%: Poor, 50-75%: Fair, 75-90%: Good, 90-100%: Excellent):
Since RQD = 64.67%, the rock stratum is classified as FAIR QUALITY ROCK.
Q.5 (c) OR 2023 7M Numerical 4x
Explain the Standard Penetration Test. What are the different corrections to be applied to observed SPT value? Following the observations of Standard Penetration Tests conducted at a site on sandy soil. Find the corrected N values. Depth: 1.50 m, Observed SPT: 12, Density: 15.5 kN/m³ Depth: 3.00 m, Observed SPT: 18, Density: 17.2 kN/m³ Depth: 4.50 m, Observed SPT: 26, Density: 19.0 kN/m³ Depth: 6.00 m, Observed SPT: 32, Density: 20.5 kN/m³
1. Standard Penetration Test & Corrections:
•
Overburden Correction:
$$C_{N} = 350 / (\sigma '_{v} + 70)$$
(per IS: 2131) and
$$N' = N \cdot C_{N}$$
(where CN ≤ 2.0).
•
Dilatancy Correction:
$$N" = 15 + 0.5 (N' - 15)$$
(applied when N' > 15 below WT).
2. Tabulation of Corrections:
•
Depth 1.50 m (N = 12, γ = 15.5 kN/m³): σ'v = 1.5 × 15.5 = 23.25 kPa.
CN = 350 / (23.25 + 70) = 350 / 93.25 = 3.75 ⇒ Cap at 2.0.
$$N' = 12 \times 2.0 = 24$$
. Dilatancy:
$$N" = 15 + 0.5(24 - 15) = \mathbf{19.5 \approx 20}$$
.
•
Depth 3.00 m (N = 18, γ = 17.2 kN/m³): σ'v = 23.25 + (1.5 × 17.2) = 23.25 + 25.8 = 49.05 kPa.
CN = 350 / (49.05 + 70) = 350 / 119.05 = 2.94 ⇒ Cap at 2.0.
$$N' = 18 \times 2.0 = 36$$
. Dilatancy:
$$N" = 15 + 0.5(36 - 15) = \mathbf{25.5 \approx 26}$$
.
•
Depth 4.50 m (N = 26, γ = 19.0 kN/m³): σ'v = 49.05 + (1.5 × 19.0) = 49.05 + 28.5 = 77.55 kPa.
CN = 350 / (77.55 + 70) = 350 / 147.55 = 2.37 ⇒ (CN ≤ 2.0 ⇒ 2.0 or √[100/77.55]=1.136). Using standard Peck/Hanson √(100/σ'v): CN = 1.136 ⇒ N' = 26 × 1.136 = 29.5 ≈ 30. Dilatancy: N" = 15 + 0.5(30 - 15) = 22.5 ≈ 23.
•
Depth 6.00 m (N = 32, γ = 20.5 kN/m³): σ'v = 77.55 + (1.5 × 20.5) = 77.55 + 30.75 = 108.3 kPa.
CN = √(100 / 108.3) = 0.961.
$$N' = 32 \times 0.961 = 30.75 \approx 31$$
. Dilatancy:
$$N" = 15 + 0.5(31 - 15) = \mathbf{23}$$
.

Unit 1 Lateral Earth Pressure 0/5
Q.1 (a) 2022 2M Numerical
Determine the depth of tension cracks developed if unsupported excavation is to be made in a soil layer of having γ = 15 kN/m³, c = 30 kN/m² and φ = 10°.
Depth of Tension Cracks Calculation:
Given Data:
Unit weight γ = 15 kN/m³, Cohesion c = 30 kN/m², Friction angle φ = 10°.
1.
Active Earth Pressure Coefficient (Ka):
$$K_a = \tan^2(45^\circ - \phi/2) = \tan^2(45^\circ - 5^\circ) = \tan^2(40^\circ) = 0.8391^2 = 0.7041$$

$$\sqrt{K_a} = 0.8391$$
2.
Depth of Tension Cracks (zc): Active lateral pressure in cohesive soil is pa = γz Ka - 2c√Ka. Tension crack depth occurs where pa = 0:
$$z_c = \frac{2c}{\gamma \sqrt{K_a}} = \frac{2 \times 30}{15 \times 0.8391} = \frac{60}{12.5865} = 4.77\text{ m}$$
3.
Final Result: Depth of tension cracks developed = 4.77 m.
(Maximum critical unsupported excavation depth Hc = 2 zc = 9.53 m).
Q.1 (b) 2022 2M Numerical
Calculate the increase in active earth pressure intensity at the bottom of 5 m retaining wall, retaining the soil of φ = 30° and γ = 18 kN/m³ due to the application of surcharge of 45 kN/m² at the top of the soil mass.
Increase in Active Earth Pressure Intensity Calculation:
Given Data:
Wall height H = 5 m, φ = 30°, γ = 18 kN/m³, Surcharge q = 45 kN/m².
1.
Active Earth Pressure Coefficient (Ka):
$$K_a = \frac{1 - \sin 30^\circ}{1 + \sin 30^\circ} = \frac{1 - 0.5}{1 + 0.5} = \frac{0.5}{1.5} = \frac{1}{3} = 0.3333$$
2.
Increase in Active Pressure Intensity (Δpa): A uniform surface surcharge q transmits a constant horizontal pressure intensity over the entire depth of the wall:
$$\Delta p_a = K_a \cdot q = \frac{1}{3} \times 45 = 15.0\text{ kN/m}^2\text{ (15\text{ kPa})}$$
3.
Final Result: Increase in active earth pressure intensity at the bottom = 15.0 kN/m².
Q.1 (c) 2022 3M Theory 2x
Explain the various assumptions made in Rankine's earth pressure theory.
Assumptions Made in Rankine's Earth Pressure Theory:
1.
Soil is homogeneous, isotropic, dry, and cohesionless (c = 0).
2.
Ground surface is a plane (horizontal or uniformly sloping).
3.
Back of the retaining wall is smooth and vertical (zero wall friction, δ = 0).
4.
Soil is in a state of plastic equilibrium throughout the failure mass.
5.
Rupture surfaces are straight planes inclined at:
$$\theta = 45^\circ + \frac{\phi}{2} \; \text{(Active)} \qquad \theta = 45^\circ - \frac{\phi}{2} \; \text{(Passive)}$$
Q.1 (d) 2022 7M Numerical 4x
A gravity retaining wall retains 15 m of a backfill γ = 20 kN/m³ and φ = 30° with a uniform horizontal backfill. Assuming the wall interface to be vertical, determine the magnitude of active and passive earth pressure and the point of action of total pressure. Assume the angle of wall friction to be 20°.
Given: H = 15 m, γ = 20 kN/m³, φ = 30°, δ = 20°, vertical back (α = 90°), horizontal fill (β = 0°).
1.
Active Condition (Coulomb Theory): For φ = 30°, δ = 20°:
$$K_{a} \approx 0.2973$$
.
Total active thrust:
$$P_{a} = 0.5 \cdot K_{a} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 0.2973 \times 20 \times 15^2 = \mathbf{668.9\text{ kN/m}}$$
.
Point of Action: Acts at H/3 = 15/3 = 5.0 m above the wall base, inclined at δ = 20° downward to the normal.
2.
Passive Condition (Coulomb Theory): For φ = 30°, δ = 20°:
$$K_{p} \approx 6.103$$
.
Total passive thrust:
$$P_{p} = 0.5 \cdot K_{p} \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2 = 0.5 \times 6.103 \times 20 \times 225 = \mathbf{13,731.8\text{ kN/m}}$$
.
Point of Action: Acts at 5.0 m above the base, inclined at 20° upward to the normal.
Q.1 (e) OR 2022 7M Theory 3x
Illustrate Rebhann's graphical construction method to evaluate the earth pressure on a retaining wall.
Rebhann's Graphical Construction & Advantages:
1.
Objective: Graphically determines Coulomb active thrust (Pa) and identifies the critical failure plane for retaining walls with wall friction (δ) and surcharge (β).
2. Construction Steps:
•
Draw wall AB and ground surface AD.
•
Draw φ-line BD at angle φ to horizontal from heel B.
•
Draw ψ-line BL at angle ψ = β - δ to line BD.
•
Draw semi-circle on BD as diameter.
•
Draw AE parallel to ψ-line, meeting BD at E.
•
Erect perpendicular EF to meet semi-circle at F.
•
With center B and radius BF, draw arc to cut BD at C.
•
Draw CD parallel to ψ-line to meet ground at D. Line BC is the failure plane.
3.
Rebhann's Diagram:
Figure: Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Thrust (Pa)
4.
Active Thrust:
$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area}(\triangle BCD)$$
5. Advantages:
•
Avoids tedious trigonometric equations.
•
Easily handles broken or irregular backfill slopes.
•
Directly identifies critical failure plane BC without trial wedges.
Unit 2 Shear Strength & Slope Stability 0/5
Q.2 (a) 2022 2M Theory
List the basic differences between a box shear test and a triaxial shear test for soils.
Differences Between Direct Shear Box Test and Triaxial Shear Test:
1.
Failure Plane: Direct shear test forces failure along a predetermined horizontal plane, whereas in a triaxial test, failure occurs along the natural weakest plane.
2.
Drainage Control: Direct shear test provides poor drainage control and cannot measure pore water pressure, whereas triaxial test provides complete drainage control and accurate pore pressure measurement.
3.
Stress Distribution: Direct shear test has non-uniform stress distribution with stress concentrations at edges, whereas triaxial test maintains uniform stress conditions throughout the cylindrical sample.
4.
Soil Applicability: Direct shear test is best suited for coarse-grained cohesionless sands, whereas triaxial test is suitable for all soil types under UU, CU, and CD conditions.
5.
Strength Parameters: Direct shear test measures total stress parameters only, whereas triaxial test determines both total and effective stress parameters.
Q.2 (b) 2022 2M Theory 4x
Describe unconsolidated undrained test and a drained test.
Unconsolidated Undrained (UU) and Consolidated Drained (CD) Tests:
1.
Unconsolidated Undrained (UU) Test: Drainage is kept closed during both the cell pressure stage and shearing stage. It is a rapid test (takes 5 to 10 minutes) with no dissipation of excess pore water pressure, measuring undrained shear strength (cu).
Example: Short-term foundation stability immediately after rapid construction on clay.
2.
Consolidated Drained (CD) Test: Drainage is kept open during both the cell pressure stage and shearing stage. It is a very slow test (takes days to weeks) allowing excess pore water pressure to fully dissipate (u = 0), measuring effective shear strength parameters (c', φ').
Example: Long-term permanent stability analysis of natural earth slopes and retaining walls.
Q.2 (c) 2022 3M Numerical
A vane, 10.8 cm long, 7.2 cm in diameter, was pressed into a soft clay at the bottom of a bore hole. Torque was applied and the value at failure was 45 N·m. Calculate the shear strength of the clay on a horizontal plane.
Given Parameters:
H = 10.8 cm = 0.108 m, D = 7.2 cm = 0.072 m, Torque T = 45 N·m.
Vane Shear Torque Formula (Shearing at both ends):
$$T = c_{u} \cdot \pi \cdot D^2 \cdot [ (H / 2) + (D / 6) ]$$

$$\pi \cdot D^2 = \pi \times (0.072)^2 = 0.016286\text{ m}^2$$
.
$$(H / 2) + (D / 6) = (0.108 / 2) + (0.072 / 6) = 0.054 + 0.012 = 0.066\text{ m}$$
.
$$T = c_{u} \times 0.016286 \times 0.066 = c_{u} \times (1.0749 \times 10⁻^3\text{ m}^3)$$
.
Undrained Shear Strength (cu):
$$c_{u} = 45 / (1.0749 \times 10⁻^3) = 41,864 N/m^2 = \mathbf{41.86\text{ kPa}}$$
.
Shear strength of clay on horizontal plane is 41.86 kN/m².
Q.2 (d) 2022 7M Numerical
A consolidated-drained triaxial test was conducted on a normally consolidated clay yielding the following data: σ₃ = 250 kN/m²; σ_d = 275 kN/m². Determine: (i) The angle of friction, (ii) Angle which the failure plane makes with the major principal plane, (iii) Normal stress and shear stress on the failure plane, (iv) Normal stress on the plane of τ_max.
Given Parameters:
Normally consolidated clay ⇒ c' = 0.
Confining stress σ'₃ = 250 kPa, Deviator stress σ_d = 275 kPa.
Major principal stress:
$$\sigma '_1 = \sigma '_3 + \sigma _d = 250 + 275 = 525\text{ kPa}$$
.
(i.
Angle of Friction (φ'): From Mohr-Coulomb for c = 0:
$$\sin \phi ' = \frac{\sigma '_1 - \sigma '_3}{\sigma '_1 + \sigma '_3} = 275 / (525 + 250) = 275 / 775 = 0.3548$$
.
$$\phi ' = \arcsin (0.3548) = \mathbf{20.78^\circ}$$
.
(ii) Failure Plane Angle with Major Principal Plane (θ):
$$\theta = 45^\circ + \phi '/2 = 45^\circ + 10.39^\circ = \mathbf{55.39^\circ}$$
.
(iii) Stresses on Failure Plane:
$$\sigma _f = [(\sigma '_1+\sigma '_3)/2] + [(\sigma '_1-\sigma '_3)/2] \cdot \cos 2\theta = 387.5 + 137.5 \cdot \cos (110.78^\circ) = 387.5 + 137.5(-0.3548) = 387.5 - 48.78 = \mathbf{338.72\text{ kPa}}$$
.
$$\tau _f = [(\sigma '_1-\sigma '_3)/2] \cdot \sin 2\theta = 137.5 \cdot \sin (110.78^\circ) = 137.5(0.9350) = \mathbf{128.56\text{ kPa}}$$
.
(Check: τ_f / σ_f = 128.56 / 338.72 = 0.3795 = tan 20.78° ✓).
(iv) Normal Stress on the Plane of τmax:
The plane of maximum shear stress occurs at 2θ = 90° (θ = 45°):
$$\sigma = (\sigma '_1 + \sigma '_3) / 2 = (525 + 250) / 2 = \mathbf{387.5\text{ kPa}}$$
(with τmax = 137.5 kPa).
Q.2 (e) OR 2022 7M Numerical
A granular soil has G = 2.70, e = 0.5 and φ = 35°. A slope has to be made of this material. If a factor of safety of 1.15 is needed against failure, determine the safe angle of slope when: (i) The slope is dry or submerged without seepage, (ii) If seepage occurs at and parallel to the surface of the slope, (iii) If seepage occurs parallel to the slope with the water table at a depth of 1.5 m, what is the factor of safety available on a slip plane parallel to the ground surface at a depth of 4 m. Assume slope angle is 30°.
Soil Parameters: G = 2.70, e = 0.5, φ = 35°, c = 0.
$$\gamma _{sat} = [\frac{G + e}{1 + e}] \cdot \gamma _{w} = [(2.7 + 0.5)/1.5] \times 9.81 = 20.93\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
$$\gamma ' = \gamma _{sat} - \gamma _{w} = 20.93 - 9.81 = 11.12\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
$$\gamma _{d} = [G / (1 + e)] \cdot \gamma _{w} = (2.7/1.5) \times 9.81 = 17.66\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
(i.
Dry or Submerged without Seepage:
$$FS = \tan \phi / \tan \beta \implies 1.15 = \tan 35^\circ / \tan \beta \implies \tan \beta = 0.7002 / 1.15 = 0.6089$$
.
Safe slope angle
$$\beta = \arctan (0.6089) = \mathbf{31.34^\circ}$$
.
(ii) Seepage Parallel to Surface at Ground Level:
$$FS = (\gamma ' / \gamma _{sat}) \cdot (\tan \phi / \tan \beta )$$
.
$$1.15 = (11.12 / 20.93) \cdot (0.7002 / \tan \beta ) = 0.5313 \times 0.7002 / \tan \beta = 0.3720 / \tan \beta$$
.
$$\tan \beta = 0.3720 / 1.15 = 0.3235 \implies \beta = \arctan (0.3235) = \mathbf{17.93^\circ}$$
.
(iii) Partially Submerged with WT at 1.5 m, Slip Plane at z = 4 m, β = 30°:
Dry/moist zone (0 to 1.5 m): ΔW₁ = 17.66 × 1.5 = 26.49 kPa.
Submerged zone (1.5 to 4 m): ΔW₂ = 20.93 × 2.5 = 52.33 kPa.
Total vertical stress σv = 26.49 + 52.33 = 78.82 kPa.
Pore water pressure u = 9.81 × 2.5 × cos² 30° = 24.53 × 0.75 = 18.40 kPa.
Normal effective stress σ' = σv cos² 30° - u = (78.82 × 0.75) - 18.40 = 59.12 - 18.40 = 40.72 kPa.
Shear stress τ = σv sin 30° cos 30° = 78.82 × 0.5 × 0.866 = 34.13 kPa.
Available Factor of Safety:
$$FS = \sigma ' \tan \phi / \tau = (40.72 \times \tan 35^\circ) / 34.13 = (40.72 \times 0.7002) / 34.13 = 28.51 / 34.13 = \mathbf{0.835 (Unstable!)}$$
.
Unit 3 Shallow Foundations 0/5
Q.3 (a) 2022 2M Theory
List the assumptions made in Terzaghi's analysis of bearing capacity of a continuous footing.
Assumptions of Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity Theory:
1.
Soil is homogeneous, isotropic, and semi-infinite.
2.
Footing is a continuous strip with infinite length (L/B → ∞), forming a two-dimensional plane-strain condition.
3.
Foundation is shallow, with depth of embedment Df ≤ width of footing B.
4.
Base of the footing is rough, preventing soil slipping along the contact surface.
5.
Soil above the foundation base level is replaced by an equivalent surcharge q = γDf (shear resistance above base level is neglected).
6.
General shear failure occurs in the supporting soil mass.
7.
Soil behaves as a rigid-plastic material obeying Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion (τ = c + σ tanφ).
Q.3 (b) 2022 2M Theory
Discuss the various factors that affect the bearing capacity of a shallow footing.
Factors Affecting Bearing Capacity of a Shallow Footing:
1.
Shear Strength of Soil (c and φ): Higher cohesion and higher angle of internal friction increase bearing capacity factors exponentially.
2.
Footing Width (B): In granular soils (sand), bearing capacity increases linearly with footing width (0.5 γ B Nγ).
3.
Depth of Embedment (Df): Deeper footing placement increases the confining surcharge pressure (γ Df Nq), directly increasing bearing capacity.
4.
Water Table Location: When groundwater rises to the foundation level, submerged unit weight (γ') replaces γ, reducing bearing capacity by up to 50%.
5.
Shape of Footing: Circular and square footings have higher bearing capacities per unit area than continuous strip footings due to 3D shape factors.
6.
Unit Weight of Soil (γ): Denser soil with higher unit weight provides greater resistance to shear displacement.
Q.3 (c) 2022 3M Theory 3x
Illustrate the effect of ground water table on the safe bearing capacity.
Ground Water Table Effect on Safe Bearing Capacity:
IS: 6403
$$q_{ult} = c N_c + \gamma_1 D_f N_q W^*_1 + 0.5 \gamma_2 B N_\gamma W^*_2$$
1.
Surcharge Correction Factor (W*1): W*1 = 0.5 [1 + dw / Df] for water table between ground level and footing base.
2.
Wedge Correction Factor (W*2): W*2 = 0.5 [1 + zw / B] for water table within depth B below footing base.
3.
Maximum Reduction: When water table rises to ground level, effective unit weight is halved (γ' ≈ 0.5 γsat), cutting bearing capacity of sand by 50%.
Q.3 (d) 2022 7M Numerical 4x
Calculate the safe bearing capacity of a square footing 1.5 m × 1.5 m, located at a depth of 1 m below the ground level in a soil of average density 20 kN/m³. φ = 20°, Nc = 17.7, Nq = 7.4, and Nγ = 5.0. Assume a suitable factor of safety and that the water table is very deep. Also compute the reduction in safe bearing capacity of the footing if the water table rises to the ground level.
Given: Square footing B = 1.5 m, Df = 1.0 m, γ = 20 kN/m³, φ = 20°, Nc = 17.7, Nq = 7.4, Nγ = 5.0. Soil is cohesionless (c = 0). Adopt FS = 3.0.
Case A: Water table very deep (Rw1 = 1.0, Rw2 = 1.0):
Terzaghi square footing (c = 0):
$$q_{ult} = \gamma D_{f} N_{q} + 0.4 \gamma B N_{\gamma } = (20 \times 1.0 \times 7.4) + (0.4 \times 20 \times 1.5 \times 5.0) = 148.0 + 60.0 = 208.0\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{nu} = q_{ult} - \gamma D_{f} = 208.0 - 20.0 = 188.0\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{safe} = (q_{nu} / 3.0) + \gamma D_{f} = (188.0 / 3.0) + 20.0 = 62.67 + 20.0 = \mathbf{82.67\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Case B: Water table rises to ground level:
Submerged unit weight
$$\gamma ' = \gamma _{sat} - \gamma _{w} = 20 - 9.81 = 10.19\text{ kN/m}^3$$
.
$$q_{ult_sub} = \gamma ' D_{f} N_{q} + 0.4 \gamma ' B N_{\gamma } = (10.19 \times 1.0 \times 7.4) + (0.4 \times 10.19 \times 1.5 \times 5.0) = 75.41 + 30.57 = 105.98\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{nu_sub} = 105.98 - (10.19 \times 1.0) = 95.79\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{safe_sub} = (95.79 / 3.0) + 10.19 = 31.93 + 10.19 = \mathbf{42.12\text{ kN/m}^2}$$
.
Percentage Reduction in Safe Bearing Capacity:
$$Reduction = [ (82.67 - 42.12) / 82.67 ] \times 100% = \mathbf{49.05%}$$
.
Q.3 (e) OR 2022 7M Numerical
A circular footing is resting on a stiff saturated clay with qu = 250 kN/m². The depth of foundation is 2 m. Determine the diameter of the footing if the column load is 600 kN. Assume a factor of safety as 2.5. The bulk unit weight of soil is 20 kN/m³.
Given Parameters:
Circular footing, Df = 2.0 m, Column load Q = 600 kN, FS = 2.5, γ = 20 kN/m³.
Saturated stiff clay (φ = 0°):
$$c = q_{u} / 2 = 250 / 2 = 125\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
1.
Terzaghi Factors for φ = 0°: Nc = 5.7, Nq = 1.0, Nγ = 0.
For a circular footing:
$$q_{ult} = 1.3 c N_{c} + \gamma D_{f} N_{q} = 1.3(125)(5.7) + (20 \times 2 \times 1) = 926.25 + 40 = 966.25\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{nu} = 926.25\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
$$q_{ns} = q_{nu} / 2.5 = 926.25 / 2.5 = 370.5\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
Safe gross pressure:
$$q_{safe} = q_{ns} + \gamma D_{f} = 370.5 + 40 = 410.5\text{ kN/m}^2$$
.
2.
Required Bearing Area & Diameter:
$$A = Q / q_{safe} = 600 / 410.5 = 1.4616\text{ m}^2$$
.
Since A = (π/4) D²:
$$D = \sqrt{ (4 \times 1.4616) / \pi } = \sqrt{1.8610} = \mathbf{1.364\text{ m}}$$
.
Provide a circular footing of diameter D = 1.40 m.
Unit 4 Deep Foundations (Piles) 0/5
Q.4 (a) 2022 2M Theory
Explain the function of pile foundation.
Functions of Pile Foundation:
1.
End-Bearing Load Transfer: Transfers heavy building loads through weak, compressible top layers down to deep stiff soil or solid bedrock.
2.
Skin Friction Load Transfer: Distributes structural loads along the surface area of the pile shaft by friction in deep uniform clay or sand strata.
3.
Resisting Uplift Forces: Anchors tall structures (transmission towers, chimneys, transmission masts) against upward tension and wind overturning moments.
4.
Resisting Lateral Loads: Resists horizontal lateral forces caused by wind, earthquakes, earth pressures, and water wave impacts on bridge piers and docks.
5.
Soil Compaction: Compaction piles densify loose granular deposits, increasing bearing capacity and mitigating earthquake liquefaction risk.
Q.4 (b) 2022 2M Theory
Discuss the basic difference in the bearing capacity computation of shallow and deep foundations.
Differences in Bearing Capacity Computation of Shallow and Deep Foundations:
1.
Load Transfer Mechanism: Shallow foundations carry load through base contact bearing pressure only (qu), whereas deep foundations (piles) carry load through both base resistance (Qb) and shaft skin friction (Qs).
2.
Surcharge Pressure: In shallow foundations, surcharge is taken as full depth q = γDf, whereas in deep foundations, effective vertical stress increases only up to a critical depth (10d to 20d) and then stays constant.
3.
Bearing Capacity Factors: Shallow foundations use Terzaghi factors (e.g., Nc = 5.7 for strip footing in clay), whereas deep foundations use deep cavity expansion factors (e.g., Nc* = 9.0 per Skempton).
4.
Failure Surface Extent: Shallow foundation failure planes extend outwards and upwards all the way to ground surface with visible heave, whereas pile failure surfaces are localized around the pile tip and shaft without ground heaving.
5.
Settlement Influence: Shallow foundations are often governed and restricted by settlement criteria, whereas deep foundations mobilize high load capacity at small settlements.
Q.4 (c) 2022 3M Numerical
A pile is driven in a uniform clay of large depth. The clay has an unconfined compression strength of 90 kN/m². The pile is 90 cm diameter and 6 m long. Determine the safe frictional resistance of the pile, assuming a factor of safety of 3. Assume the adhesion factor α = 0.7.
Given Parameters:
Clay qu = 90 kPa ⇒ c = qu / 2 = 45 kPa.
Pile diameter d = 0.90 m, Length L = 6.0 m, Adhesion factor α = 0.7, FS = 3.
1.
Surface Area of Pile Shaft (As):
$$A_{s} = \pi \cdot d \cdot L = \pi \times 0.90 \times 6.0 = 16.965\text{ m}^2$$
.
2.
Ultimate Skin Friction Resistance (Qs):
$$Q_{s} = \alpha \cdot c \cdot A_{s} = 0.7 \times 45 \times 16.965 = \mathbf{534.40\text{ kN}}$$
.
3.
Safe Frictional Resistance:
$$Q_{safe_friction} = Q_{s} / FS = 534.40 / 3.0 = \mathbf{178.13\text{ kN}}$$
.
Q.4 (d) 2022 7M Numerical
A 12 m long, 300 mm diameter pile is driven in a uniform deposit of sand (φ = 40°). The water table is at a great depth and is not likely to rise. The average dry unit weight of sand is 18 kN/m³. Using Nq = 137, calculate the safe load capacity of the pile with a factor of safety of 2.5.
Given Parameters:
L = 12 m, d = 0.30 m, γ = 18 kN/m³, φ = 40°, Nq = 137, FS = 2.5.
1.
Base Resistance (Qb): Base area Ab = (π/4)(0.3)² = 0.07068 m².
Critical depth in dense sand: Lc ≈ 15 d = 15(0.3) = 4.5 m (or 20 d = 6.0 m).
At critical depth Lc = 15 d = 4.5 m, effective overburden reaches limiting value:
$$\sigma '_{v} = \gamma \cdot L_{c} = 18 \times 4.5 = 81.0\text{ kPa}$$
.
Limiting unit base resistance:
$$q_{b} = \sigma '_{v} \cdot N_{q} = 81.0 \times 137 = 11,097\text{ kPa}$$
.
$$Q_{b} = q_{b} \cdot A_{b} = 11,097 \times 0.07068 = \mathbf{784.3\text{ kN}}$$
.
2.
Shaft Resistance (Qs): For φ = 40°, earth pressure coefficient K ≈ 1.0, wall friction δ ≈ 0.75 φ = 30°.
Average vertical stress along shaft from 0 to 4.5 m:
$$\sigma _{v1} = 0.5(81) = 40.5\text{ kPa}$$
.
Average vertical stress from 4.5 to 12 m (capped):
$$\sigma _{v2} = 81.0\text{ kPa}$$
.
$$f_{s1} = K \sigma _{v1} \tan \delta = 1.0(40.5) \tan 30^\circ = 23.38\text{ kPa}$$
over As1 = π(0.3)(4.5) = 4.241 m² ⇒ Qs1 = 99.1 kN.
$$f_{s2} = K \sigma _{v2} \tan \delta = 1.0(81.0) \tan 30^\circ = 46.76\text{ kPa}$$
over As2 = π(0.3)(7.5) = 7.068 m² ⇒ Qs2 = 330.5 kN.
Total skin friction:
$$Q_{s} = 99.1 + 330.5 = \mathbf{429.6\text{ kN}}$$
.
3.
Total Safe Capacity:
$$Q_{u} = Q_{b} + Q_{s} = 784.3 + 429.6 = 1213.9\text{ kN}$$
.
$$Q_{safe} = Q_{u} / FS = 1213.9 / 2.5 = \mathbf{485.56\text{ kN}}$$
.
Q.4 (e) OR 2022 7M Numerical 2x
A square group of 9 piles was driven into soft clay extending to a large depth. The diameter and length of the piles were 30 cm and 9 m respectively. If the unconfined compression strength of the clay is 90 kN/m², and the pile spacing is 90 cm centre to centre. Calculate the capacity of the pile group? Assume a factor of safety of 2.5 and adhesion factor of 0.75.
Given Parameters:
3 × 3 array (n = 9), d = 0.3 m, L = 9 m, s = 0.9 m, qu = 90 kPa ⇒ c = 45 kPa, α = 0.75, FS = 2.5.
1.
Individual Pile Failure: Ab = (π/4)(0.3)² = 0.07068 m², As = π(0.3)(9) = 8.482 m².
Single pile:
$$Q_{u} = 9(45)(0.07068) + 0.75(45)(8.482) = 28.63 + 286.28 = 314.91\text{ kN}$$
.
Total for group:
$$Q_{gi} = 9 \times 314.91 = \mathbf{2834.2\text{ kN}}$$
.
2.
Block Failure: Block width B = 2s + d = 2(0.9) + 0.3 = 2.1 m.
$$Q_{gb} = 9 c B^2 + 4 B L c = 9(45)(2.1^2) + 4(2.1)(9)(45) = 1786.05 + 3402.0 = \mathbf{5188.05\text{ kN}}$$
.
3.
Governing Capacity: Governing ultimate Qug = min(2834.2, 5188.05) = 2834.2 kN.
Safe capacity = 2834.2 / 2.5 = 1133.68 kN.
Unit 5 Soil Exploration & Testing 0/5
Q.5 (a) 2022 2M Theory
List the laboratory and field tests used for the soil investigation work.
Laboratory and Field Tests in Soil Investigation:
1. Field (In-Situ) Tests:
•
Standard Penetration Test (SPT): Determines N-value, relative density of sands, and consistency of clays.
•
Cone Penetration Test (CPT): Measures point resistance and sleeve friction continuously with depth.
•
Plate Load Test (PLT): Evaluates ultimate bearing capacity and settlement of footings in-situ.
•
Field Vane Shear Test: Determines in-situ undrained shear strength of soft cohesive soils.
2. Laboratory Tests:
•
Grain Size Analysis: Sieve analysis and hydrometer test for soil classification.
•
Atterberg Limits: Liquid limit and plastic limit tests to determine soil plasticity.
•
Shear Strength Tests: Direct shear box test and triaxial shear test (UU, CU, CD) to find c and φ.
•
Consolidation Test: Oedometer test to determine compression index and rate of settlement.
Q.5 (b) 2022 2M Theory 2x
Describe the purpose of soil investigation.
Purpose of Soil Investigation:
1.
Foundation Selection: To determine the most suitable, safe, and economical type and depth of foundation for the proposed structure.
2.
Bearing Capacity Evaluation: To calculate the safe bearing capacity of soil to prevent shear failure under building loads.
3.
Settlement Prediction: To estimate total and differential settlements and ensure they remain within permissible structural limits.
4.
Earth Pressure Assessment: To provide design parameters (Ka, Kp) for retaining walls, basement walls, and temporary shoring.
5.
Groundwater Observation: To locate the groundwater table and its seasonal fluctuations, identifying dewatering and waterproofing requirements.
6.
Construction Risk Mitigation: To identify problematic soils (expansive Black Cotton soil, collapsible soils, high water seepage) before construction begins.
Q.5 (c) 2022 3M Numerical 2x
Calculate the area ratio of a thin walled tube sampler having an external diameter of 6 cm and a wall thickness of 2.25 mm. Do you recommend the sampler for obtaining undisturbed soil samples? Why?
Given: External diameter D2 = 6.0 cm = 60.0 mm, Wall thickness t = 2.25 mm.
1.
Internal Diameter (D1):
$$D_{1} = D_{2} - 2t = 60.0 - 2(2.25) = 60.0 - 4.5 = \mathbf{55.5\text{ mm}}$$
.
2.
Area Ratio (Ar):
$$A_{r} = [ (D_{2}^2 - D_{1}^2) / D_{1}^2 ] \times 100%$$

$$D_{2}^2 = 60^2 = 3600\text{ mm}^2, D_{1}^2 = 55.5^2 = 3080.25\text{ mm}^2$$
.
$$A_{r} = [ (3600 - 3080.25) / 3080.25 ] \times 100% = [ 519.75 / 3080.25 ] \times 100% = \mathbf{16.87%}$$
.
3. Recommendation & Justification:
Recommendation: Yes, this sampler is acceptable for obtaining good quality undisturbed samples in cohesive soils. Per IS: 1892, an area ratio ≤ 10% is ideal for extremely sensitive soils, but Ar up to 20% is permissible in normal medium-to-stiff clays. Because 16.87% < 20%, minimal soil displacement occurs, keeping perimeter edge disturbance low.
Q.5 (d) 2022 7M Theory 4x
Illustrate the standard penetration test used in soil exploration. List the information that can be obtained by the test when made in (a) clay (b) sand. Comment on the correction factors to be used for calculating N.
Standard Penetration Test (SPT) & Information Obtained:
IS: 2131
1.
Test Procedure: Split-spoon sampler (50.8 mm OD, 35 mm ID) driven into borehole bottom by 63.5 kg hammer falling 750 mm. Blows for last 300 mm = Observed N-value.
Figure: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) Setup per IS: 2131
2. Corrections:
•
Overburden: N' = N0 × [350 / (σ'v + 70)] for σ'v ≤ 280 kPa.
•
Dilatancy: N'' = 15 + 0.5 (N' - 15) for saturated fine sand/silt when N' > 15.
3. Information Obtained:
•
Sand: Relative density Dr (N < 4 Very loose to N > 50 Very dense), friction angle φ ≈ 27.1° + 0.3 N', liquefaction risk.
•
Clay: Unconfined compressive strength qu ≈ 12.5 N (kPa), consistency.
•
Design: Safe bearing capacity of footings and pile capacities.
Q.5 (e) OR 2022 7M Theory 3x
Classify the various methods of soil exploration and mention the circumstances under which each is best situated.
Classification of Soil Exploration Methods & Circumstances:
IS: 1892
Method Description Best Suited Circumstances
1. Open Test Pits Shallow manual or backhoe excavation (up to 3-5 m). Shallow foundation sites; enables direct visual inspection and block sampling.
2. Auger Boring Hand or power auger turned into ground. Cohesive clays and silts above water table (up to 10-15 m depth).
3. Wash Boring Water jet chops soil inside casing. Sands and soft clays below water table; unsuitable for rock.
4. Rotary Core Drilling Rotating diamond core barrel with drilling mud. Medium to hard rock and boulders; recovers continuous rock cores (RQD).
5. Percussion Drilling Heavy drill bit dropped repeatedly to crush soil. Bouldery, stony ground and hard glacial till.
6. Geophysical Methods Seismic refraction and electrical resistivity. Rapid preliminary reconnaissance of large sites (highways, dams, pipelines).

Rankine Active Earth Pressure & Tension Crack Depth

$$p_a = K_a \sigma'_v - 2c \sqrt{K_a}$$

Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$p_a$Active lateral earth pressurekPa
$K_a$Rankine active pressure coefficientdimensionless
$\sigma'_v$Effective vertical overburden stress (\gamma z)kPa

Unit 1 Core Numerical / Theory

Rankine Passive Earth Pressure Coefficient

$$p_p = K_p \sigma'_v + 2c \sqrt{K_p}$$
$$K_p = \frac{1 + \sin\phi}{1 - \sin\phi} = \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{K_a}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$p_p$Passive lateral earth resistancekPa
$K_p$Rankine passive earth coefficientdimensionless
$\sigma'_v$Effective vertical overburden stresskPa
$c$Cohesion interceptkPa
Exam Insight: Passive pressure represents the maximum resisting force when a wall is pushed into backfill. Full mobilization requires 4 to 10 times greater wall displacement than active state.
Unit 1 75% (3/4 Papers - 7M Numerical)

Coulomb Earth Thrust on Gravity Retaining Walls

$$P_a = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 K_a \qquad P_p = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 K_p$$
$$K_a = \frac{\cos^2\phi}{\cos\delta \left[ 1 + \sqrt{\frac{\sin(\phi+\delta)\sin\phi}{\cos\delta}} \right]^2} \quad (\text{for } \alpha=90^\circ, \beta=0^\circ)$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$P_a, P_p$Total active / passive thrust per lineal metrekN/m
$H$Total vertical height of retaining wallm
$\delta$Angle of wall interface friction (typically 20° or 2/3 φ)degrees
$\gamma$Unit weight of backfill soilkN/m³
Exam Insight: Thrust acts at H/3 from the base, inclined at angle δ to the normal of the wall face (downward for active, upward for passive). For vertical smooth walls (δ=0, α=90°), Coulomb's equation reduces identically to Rankine's formula.
Unit 1 Core Theory Derivation

At-Rest Earth Pressure Coefficient (Elastic & Empirical)

$$K_0 = \frac{\mu}{1 - \mu} \quad (\text{Elastic Theory}) \qquad K_0 = 1 - \sin\phi \quad (\text{Jaky's Equation})$$
$$\sigma_h = K_0 \cdot \sigma'_v \qquad \text{Condition: } \varepsilon_x = \varepsilon_y = 0 \text{ (Zero Lateral Yield)}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$K_0$Coefficient of earth pressure at restdimensionless
$\mu$Poisson's ratio of soil (typically 0.25 - 0.35)dimensionless
$\sigma_h$At-rest horizontal lateral effective stresskPa
$\phi$Effective friction angle of normally consolidated soildegrees
Exam Insight: Derived from Hooke's 3D law by setting lateral strain ε_x = (1/E)[σ_x - μ(σ_y + σ_z)] = 0. Governs rigid unyielding structures like basement walls keyed into bedrock and bridge abutments on fixed piles.

Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Earth Thrust

$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area}(\Delta BGH) = \frac{1}{2}\gamma \cdot (GH \cdot BG \sin\psi)$$
$$\text{Critical Rupture Criterion: } GH = \frac{BG}{\sin\psi} \iff \frac{dP_a}{d\theta} = 0$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$P_a$Total active thrust from sliding wedgekN/m
$\Delta BGH$Earth pressure triangle constructed on rupture planem²
$\psi$Inclination angle between ground and rupture planedegrees
Exam Insight: Poncelet's semicircle theorem geometrically maximizes the trial wedge thrust without solving complex differential calculus. Critical rupture surface AH isolates the failure wedge.

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion & Principal Stress Relation

$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) + 2c'\tan\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right)$$

Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:

$\sigma'_3$Minor effective principal stress (cell confining pressure)kPa
$c'$Effective cohesion interceptkPa
$\phi'$Effective angle of internal frictiondegrees
$N_\phi$Flow value parameter tan²(45° + φ'/2)dimensionless
$\theta_{\text{cr}}$Critical shear failure angle with major principal planedegrees
Exam Insight: Fundamental governing equation for triaxial shear tests, unconfined compression tests, and direct shear tests. For purely cohesive soil (φ=0): σ₁ - σ₃ = 2c_u = q_u. For cohesionless sand (c=0): σ'₁/σ'₃ = tan²(45° + φ'/2).

Triaxial Specimen Area Correction (Axial Strain)

$$A = \frac{A_0}{1 - \varepsilon} \qquad \text{where } \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0}$$
$$\Delta\sigma = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3 = \frac{\text{Failure Deviator Load}}{A} \qquad A_0 = \frac{\pi}{4} D_0^2$$

$A_0$Initial cross-sectional area before shearingm²

$$FS = \frac{c' + \gamma' z \cos^2\beta \tan\phi'}{\gamma_{\text{sat}} z \sin\beta \cos\beta}$$

$$T = c_u \pi D^2 \left( \frac{H}{2} + \frac{D}{6} \right) \implies c_u = \frac{T}{\pi D^2 \left( \frac{H}{2} + \frac{D}{6} \right)}$$

$$q_{\text{ult}} = c N_c + \gamma D_f N_q R_{w1} + \frac{1}{2} \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2}$$
$$\text{Square: } q_{\text{ult}} = 1.3 c N_c + q N_q R_{w1} + 0.4 \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2} \qquad \text{Circular: } 1.3 c N_c + q N_q R_{w1} + 0.3 \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2}$$

$c$Soil cohesion interceptkPa

$D_f$Depth of foundation footing below ground surfacem

Water Table Correction Factors (Rw1 & Rw2)

$$R_{w1} = 0.5 \left( 1 + \frac{z_{w1}}{D_f} \right) \qquad R_{w2} = 0.5 \left( 1 + \frac{z_{w2}}{B} \right)$$
$$\text{Boundary Limits: } 0.5 \le R_{w1}, R_{w2} \le 1.0 \qquad \text{At Ground Level: } R_{w1} = R_{w2} = 0.5$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$R_{w1}$Surcharge water table reduction factor (modifies γ D_f N_q)dimensionless
$R_{w2}$Wedge zone water table reduction factor (modifies 0.5 γ B N_γ)dimensionless

Housel's Two-Plate Method for Foundation Bearing Capacity

$$Q_1 = A_1 m + P_1 n \qquad Q_2 = A_2 m + P_2 n$$
$$Q_F = A_F \cdot m + P_F \cdot n \quad (\text{Prototype Foundation Permissible Load})$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$Q_1, Q_2$Test loads on plate 1 and plate 2 at permissible settlementkN
$A_1, A_2$Contact surface areas of test plates 1 and 2m²
$P_1, P_2$Perimeters of test plates 1 and 2m
$m$Perimeter shear factor (side shear mobilization)kN/m
$n$Direct bearing factor (base pressure mobilization)kN/m²
$Q_F$Allowable design load of full-scale prototype footingkN
Exam Insight: Housel's method bypasses plate size extrapolation errors by testing two plates of different sizes (e.g. 30 cm and 60 cm) at the identical permissible settlement, solving simultaneous equations for m and n.
Unit 3 Core Numerical / Theory

Immediate (Elastic) Settlement of Shallow Footings

$$S_i = \frac{q B (1 - \mu^2)}{E_s} \cdot I_f$$
$$\text{Rigid Footing: } I_f \approx 0.82 \qquad \text{Center of Flexible Footing: } I_f \approx 1.12 \text{ (Square)}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$S_i$Immediate elastic settlement under foundation loadm (or mm)
$q$Net foundation contact pressurekPa
$B$Characteristic footing width / diameterm
$\mu$Poisson's ratio of foundation soildimensionless
$E_s$Modulus of elasticity of soil depositkPa
$I_f$Influence shape and rigidity factordimensionless
Exam Insight: Calculates instantaneous elastic distortion occurring before primary consolidation. Critical for sand deposits and initial settlement in stiff clay layers.
Unit 4 100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M)

Single Driven / Bored Pile Capacity in Cohesive Soil

$$Q_u = Q_b + Q_s = 9 c_u A_b + \alpha \bar{c}_u A_s$$
$$A_b = \frac{\pi d^2}{4} \qquad A_s = \pi d L \qquad Q_{\text{safe}} = \frac{Q_u}{\text{FS}}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$Q_u$Ultimate single pile axial compressive capacitykN
$Q_b$Base end-bearing resistance (N_c = 9 per Skempton)kN
$Q_s$Shaft skin friction resistance along pile perimeterkN
$c_u$Undrained cohesion at pile base tipkPa
$\bar{c}_u$Average undrained cohesion along pile shaft embedmentkPa
$\alpha$Adhesion factor between clay and pile material (0.4 - 0.8)dimensionless
$d$Pile diameterm
$L$Embedded pile lengthm
Exam Insight: Adopt factor of safety FS = 2.5 to 3.0. In soft clay, skin friction Q_s typically accounts for 80-90% of total single pile capacity. For piles driven in sand: Q_u = σ'_v N_q A_b + K_s σ'_v tanδ A_s.
Unit 4 100% Guaranteed (Verbatim 2024 Q4d & 2022 Q4e - 7M)

Pile Group Block Failure Capacity in Soft Clay

$$Q_{\text{ug}} = 9 c_u B^2 + 4 B L \bar{c}_u$$
$$B = (n_1 - 1)s + d \qquad Q_{\text{safe, group}} = \frac{\min(Q_{\text{ug}}, \, n \cdot Q_u)}{\text{FS}}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$Q_{\text{ug}}$Ultimate block failure capacity of entire pile group masskN
$B$Overall width of square pile group block perimeterm
$s$Center-to-center pile spacingm
$d$Individual pile diameterm
$n_1$Number of piles in one row (e.g. 3 for a 3x3 group)count
$n$Total number of piles in group (n = n_1²)count
$L$Embedded length of pilesm
$c_u$Undrained cohesion of claykPa
Exam Insight: Notice that for block shear, adhesion factor α = 1.0 because failure occurs soil-on-soil along the outer block envelope, not pile-to-soil. Safe group capacity is ALWAYS the smaller of block capacity and individual sum divided by FS.
Unit 4 75% (3/4 Papers - 6-7M Derivation)

Optimum Pile Spacing in Cohesive Soil

$$s = d + \frac{2d}{\pi \alpha}$$
$$\text{Derivation Condition: } \text{Block Skin Friction Perimeter} = \sum \text{Individual Pile Skin Friction}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$s$Optimum center-to-center pile spacingm
$d$Diameter of pilem
$\alpha$Pile-soil adhesion factor (typically 0.6 - 0.8)dimensionless
Exam Insight: Equating group perimeter capacity 4BL c_u to n individual friction sum n(πα d L c_u) yields s = d + (2d / πα). For α = 0.7, s ≈ 2.5d to 3.0d, perfectly matching standard Indian Standard spacing guidelines (s ≥ 2.5d to 3d).
Unit 4 Core Numerical / Theory

Converse-Labarre Pile Group Efficiency Formula

$$\eta = 1 - \frac{\theta}{90^\circ} \left[ \frac{(m-1)n + (n-1)m}{m \cdot n} \right]$$
$$\text{where } \theta = \arctan\left(\frac{d}{s}\right) \text{ (in degrees)} \qquad Q_{\text{group}} = \eta \cdot n \cdot Q_{\text{single}}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$\eta$Group efficiency factor (typically 0.65 - 0.85 for clays)fraction / %
$m, n$Number of pile rows and columns in rectangular groupcount
$d$Diameter of pilem
$s$Center-to-center pile spacingm
$\theta$Overlap interference angle arctan(d/s)degrees
Exam Insight: Reflects overlapping stress bulbs between adjacent piles. In friction piles driven in dense sand, soil compaction can cause η > 1.0. In clays, overlapping shear zones always reduce capacity (η < 1.0).
Unit 5 100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M Numerical)

SPT Overburden Pressure Correction (CN)

$$N' = N \cdot C_N = N \cdot \left[ \frac{350}{\sigma'_v + 70} \right] \quad (\text{per IS: 2131})$$
$$\text{Constraint: } C_N \le 2.0 \quad (\sigma'_v \le 280\text{ kPa}) \qquad \text{Peck & Hanson: } N' = N \cdot \sqrt{\frac{100}{\sigma'_v}}$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$N$Observed field SPT blow count for final 300 mm driveblows / 300 mm
$N'$Overburden-corrected SPT blow countblows / 300 mm
$C_N$Overburden correction factor (capped at 2.0)dimensionless
$\sigma'_v$Effective vertical overburden stress at test elevationkPa
Exam Insight: Low confining stress at shallow depths artificially underestimates density; deep overburden artificially overestimates blow counts. Must always be calculated and applied BEFORE dilatancy correction.
Unit 5 100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M Numerical)

SPT Dilatancy Correction (Terzaghi & Peck)

$$N'' = 15 + \frac{1}{2}(N' - 15) \qquad (\text{Applied when } N' > 15 \text{ below WT})$$
$$\text{Condition: Fine saturated sand or silty sand below groundwater table with } N' > 15$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$N''$Final design SPT blow count after dilatancy correctionblows / 300 mm
$N'$Overburden-corrected blow count from Step 1blows / 300 mm
Exam Insight: In saturated fine sand/silt, rapid hammer impacts cause dynamic volume expansion (dilatancy), creating transient negative pore water pressures that falsely increase shear resistance and blow counts. The dilatancy correction removes this non-conservative artifact.
Unit 5 100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 3-7M)

Soil Sampler Design Criteria (Ar, Ci, Co)

$$A_r = \frac{D_{\text{ext}}^2 - D_{\text{int}}^2}{D_{\text{int}}^2} \times 100\%$$
$$C_i = \frac{D_s - D_c}{D_c} \times 100\% \quad (1\%\text{--}3\%) \qquad C_o = \frac{D_w - D_t}{D_t} \times 100\% \quad (0\%\text{--}2\%)$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$A_r$Area ratio of sampler cutting edge (disturbed vs undisturbed indicator)%
$C_i$Inside clearance ratio (prevents tube friction & internal swelling)%
$C_o$Outside clearance ratio (reduces outside driving resistance)%
$D_{\text{ext}}$External diameter of cutting shoemm
$D_{\text{int}}$Internal diameter of cutting edge orificemm
$D_s$Internal diameter of main sampler liner tubemm
Exam Insight: For undisturbed sampling in soft/sensitive clay: A_r must be ≤ 10% to 12% (thin-walled Shelby tube). Thick-walled split-spoon samplers have A_r ≈ 30-45%, producing heavily disturbed samples suitable only for index classification.
Unit 5 Core Practical / Theory (3/4 Papers)

Rock Quality Designation (RQD) & Core Recovery

$$\text{RQD} = \frac{\sum (\text{Length of sound core pieces } \ge 10\text{ cm})}{\text{Total core drill run length}} \times 100\%$$
$$\text{TCR (Total Core Recovery)} = \frac{\text{Total recovered core length}}{\text{Total run length}} \times 100\%$$
Parameter Breakdown & SI Units:
$\text{RQD}$Rock Quality Designation index percentage%
$\text{TCR}$Total Core Recovery ratio%
$L_{\text{core}}$Individual sound cylindrical rock core piece lengthcm / mm
Exam Insight: Standard Deere classification: RQD < 25% (Very Poor), 25-50% (Poor), 50-75% (Fair), 75-90% (Good), 90-100% (Excellent). Pieces showing mechanical breaks from drilling must be fitted together as a single intact piece.
Unit Topic & Application Governing Equation Parameter Definitions & Units
Unit 1 Rankine Active Earth Pressure & Tension Crack Depth
100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers)
$$p_a = K_a \sigma'_v - 2c \sqrt{K_a}$$
$$K_a = \frac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi} = \tan^2\left(45^\circ - \frac{\phi}{2}\right) \qquad z_c = \frac{2c}{\gamma \sqrt{K_a}}$$
At ground surface (z = 0), p_a = -2c√K_a (tensile zone). Tension crack develops to depth z_c. Total net active thrust before water enters crack is P_a = 0.5 K_a γ (H - z_c)² acting at (H - z_c)/3 from the base. Depth of zero net pressure is 2z_c.
Unit 1 Rankine Passive Earth Pressure Coefficient
Core Numerical / Theory
$$p_p = K_p \sigma'_v + 2c \sqrt{K_p}$$
$$K_p = \frac{1 + \sin\phi}{1 - \sin\phi} = \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{K_a}$$
Passive pressure represents the maximum resisting force when a wall is pushed into backfill. Full mobilization requires 4 to 10 times greater wall displacement than active state.
Unit 1 Coulomb Earth Thrust on Gravity Retaining Walls
75% (3/4 Papers - 7M Numerical)
$$P_a = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 K_a \qquad P_p = \frac{1}{2} \gamma H^2 K_p$$
$$K_a = \frac{\cos^2\phi}{\cos\delta \left[ 1 + \sqrt{\frac{\sin(\phi+\delta)\sin\phi}{\cos\delta}} \right]^2} \quad (\text{for } \alpha=90^\circ, \beta=0^\circ)$$
Thrust acts at H/3 from the base, inclined at angle δ to the normal of the wall face (downward for active, upward for passive). For vertical smooth walls (δ=0, α=90°), Coulomb's equation reduces identically to Rankine's formula.
Unit 1 At-Rest Earth Pressure Coefficient (Elastic & Empirical)
Core Theory Derivation
$$K_0 = \frac{\mu}{1 - \mu} \quad (\text{Elastic Theory}) \qquad K_0 = 1 - \sin\phi \quad (\text{Jaky's Equation})$$
$$\sigma_h = K_0 \cdot \sigma'_v \qquad \text{Condition: } \varepsilon_x = \varepsilon_y = 0 \text{ (Zero Lateral Yield)}$$
Derived from Hooke's 3D law by setting lateral strain ε_x = (1/E)[σ_x - μ(σ_y + σ_z)] = 0. Governs rigid unyielding structures like basement walls keyed into bedrock and bridge abutments on fixed piles.
Unit 1 Rebhann's Graphical Construction for Active Earth Thrust
75% (3/4 Papers - 6-7M Derivation)
$$P_a = \gamma \cdot \text{Area}(\Delta BGH) = \frac{1}{2}\gamma \cdot (GH \cdot BG \sin\psi)$$
$$\text{Critical Rupture Criterion: } GH = \frac{BG}{\sin\psi} \iff \frac{dP_a}{d\theta} = 0$$
Poncelet's semicircle theorem geometrically maximizes the trial wedge thrust without solving complex differential calculus. Critical rupture surface AH isolates the failure wedge.
Unit 2 Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion & Principal Stress Relation
100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M)
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right) + 2c'\tan\left(45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2}\right)$$
$$\sigma'_1 = \sigma'_3 N_\phi + 2c'\sqrt{N_\phi} \qquad \theta_{\text{cr}} = 45^\circ + \frac{\phi'}{2} \quad (\text{Failure Plane Angle})$$
Fundamental governing equation for triaxial shear tests, unconfined compression tests, and direct shear tests. For purely cohesive soil (φ=0): σ₁ - σ₃ = 2c_u = q_u. For cohesionless sand (c=0): σ'₁/σ'₃ = tan²(45° + φ'/2).
Unit 2 Triaxial Specimen Area Correction (Axial Strain)
Core Numerical Step (Every Triaxial Problem)
$$A = \frac{A_0}{1 - \varepsilon} \qquad \text{where } \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0}$$
$$\Delta\sigma = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3 = \frac{\text{Failure Deviator Load}}{A} \qquad A_0 = \frac{\pi}{4} D_0^2$$
Assumes cylindrical specimen deforms as a right cylinder with zero net volume change during undrained shear (or uniform lateral bulging). Forgetting area correction falsely overestimates deviator stress by 10-25%.
Unit 2 Infinite Slope Stability with Steady Seepage Parallel to Slope
100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M)
$$FS = \frac{c' + \gamma' z \cos^2\beta \tan\phi'}{\gamma_{\text{sat}} z \sin\beta \cos\beta}$$
$$\text{For granular soil } (c'=0): \quad FS = \frac{\gamma'}{\gamma_{\text{sat}}} \cdot \frac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta} \approx 0.5 \cdot \frac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta}$$
Seepage force parallel to the slope cuts effective normal stress by roughly half, dropping the factor of safety of granular slopes by ~50% compared to dry conditions (FS_dry = tanφ'/tanβ).
Unit 2 Vane Shear Test: Undrained Cohesion Formula
Core Practical / Theory (3/4 Papers)
$$T = c_u \pi D^2 \left( \frac{H}{2} + \frac{D}{6} \right) \implies c_u = \frac{T}{\pi D^2 \left( \frac{H}{2} + \frac{D}{6} \right)}$$
$$\text{If top end not submerged: } \quad T = c_u \pi D^2 \left( \frac{H}{2} + \frac{D}{12} \right)$$
Used exclusively for in-situ testing of very soft to soft saturated clays where undisturbed sampling is virtually impossible. Standard lab vane: D = 12 mm, H = 24 mm. Field vane: D = 50-100 mm.
Unit 3 Terzaghi Ultimate Bearing Capacity Equation
100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M Numerical)
$$q_{\text{ult}} = c N_c + \gamma D_f N_q R_{w1} + \frac{1}{2} \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2}$$
$$\text{Square: } q_{\text{ult}} = 1.3 c N_c + q N_q R_{w1} + 0.4 \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2} \qquad \text{Circular: } 1.3 c N_c + q N_q R_{w1} + 0.3 \gamma B N_\gamma R_{w2}$$
Safe bearing capacity: q_safe = (q_ult - γ D_f)/FS + γ D_f. For pure cohesive clay (φ=0): N_c = 5.7, N_q = 1.0, N_γ = 0. For general shear failure; for local shear failure, use c' = (2/3)c and tanφ' = (2/3)tanφ.
Unit 3 Water Table Correction Factors (Rw1 & Rw2)
100% Guaranteed (4/4 Papers - 7M)
$$R_{w1} = 0.5 \left( 1 + \frac{z_{w1}}{D_f} \right) \qquad R_{w2} = 0.5 \left( 1 + \frac{z_{w2}}{B} \right)$$
$$\text{Boundary Limits: } 0.5 \le R_{w1}, R_{w2} \le 1.0 \qquad \text{At Ground Level: } R_{w1} = R_{w2} = 0.5$$
When water table rises from deep below (depth > D_f + B) to the ground surface, both R_w1 and R_w2 drop from 1.0 to 0.5, halving both surcharge resistance and shear wedge resistance (~50% capacity loss).
Unit 3 Housel's Two-Plate Method for Foundation Bearing Capacity
Core Numerical / Theory (3/4 Papers)
$$Q_1 = A_1 m + P_1 n \qquad Q_2 = A_2 m + P_2 n$$
$$Q_F = A_F \cdot m + P_F \cdot n \quad (\text{Prototype Foundation Permissible Load})$$
Housel's method bypasses plate size extrapolation errors by testing two plates of different sizes (e.g. 30 cm and 60 cm) at the identical permissible settlement, solving simultaneous equations for m and n.

Calculates instantaneous elastic distortion occurring before primary consolidation. Critical for sand deposits and initial settlement in stiff clay layers.

Adopt factor of safety FS = 2.5 to 3.0. In soft clay, skin friction Q_s typically accounts for 80-90% of total single pile capacity. For piles driven in sand: Q_u = σ'_v N_q A_b + K_s σ'_v tanδ A_s.

Unit 4 Converse-Labarre Pile Group Efficiency Formula
Core Numerical / Theory
$$\eta = 1 - \frac{\theta}{90^\circ} \left[ \frac{(m-1)n + (n-1)m}{m \cdot n} \right]$$

Reflects overlapping stress bulbs between adjacent piles. In friction piles driven in dense sand, soil compaction can cause η > 1.0. In clays, overlapping shear zones always reduce capacity (η < 1.0).
